**Eligibility Requirements**
Youth must meet HUD FYI/FUP youth criteria: age 18 through 24, left foster care or will leave foster care within 90 days, and homeless or at risk of homelessness. HUD states the public child-welfare agency refers eligible youth to the PHA, which then determines Housing Choice Voucher eligibility. Housing Connect announced 52 FYI vouchers for youth ages 18-24 who left or are transitioning from foster care and are homeless or at risk. Sources: https://housingconnect.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Press-Release-FYI-vouchers-2024_Redacted.pdf and https://www.hud.gov/helping-americans/housing-choice-vouchers-family

**How to Best Connect**
This is not a general open waitlist. Youth should work with DCFS/public child-welfare, youth homeless service providers, or Housing Connect agency-referral partners so the required referral can be made. Housing Connect general contact is 801-284-4400; Housing Connect’s site also has an agency-referral portal at https://housingconnect.org/connect-to-housing/.

**Access**
Housing Connect serves low- and moderate-income households in Salt Lake County. FYI vouchers provide rental assistance in the private market when a voucher is issued and leased; the 2024 award notice said vouchers were available for use beginning December 1, 2024. General Housing Connect waiting lists may be closed even when agency-referred special vouchers exist.

**Important Information to Know**
HUD describes youth vouchers as limited to 36 months, with possible extension up to 24 additional months under FSHO requirements. Voucher availability, referral sequencing, supportive-service requirements, documentation, and leasing timelines should be confirmed before relying on the program. This is rental assistance, not emergency shelter.

contentRevisions.before:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicant must be responsible for the utilities, live in Salt Lake County or Tooele County for UCA service, and have household income at or below 150% of the federal poverty level. At least one household member must be a U.S. citizen or qualified non-citizen. Required documents include USCIS legal-status documents when applicable, Social Security cards or a birth certificate for a child under 12 months, recent power and gas bills, and prior-month proof of income for all adults. Source: https://utahca.org/heat-utility-assistance/

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-359-2444 to schedule a phone appointment or get application help. Applicants may apply online, email HEAT@utahca.org, mail the application to 1307 S 900 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84104, or use the drop-off location at 3060 S Lester St, West Valley City, UT 84119. For Rocky Mountain Power HELP questions, UCA also lists 844-214-3090.

**Access**
UCA's intake line is posted as Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM. HEAT assists with power and gas bills year-round and offers crisis assistance year-round for qualifying households with a qualified crisis and 48-hour shutoff notice. Seasonal assistance is once per season, October 1 through September 30. If a Rocky Mountain Power account receives a HEAT benefit, the household is automatically enrolled in HELP monthly electric-bill discounts for the next 12 months.

**Important Information to Know**
Water assistance is limited. UCA says ordinary processing can take 6-8 weeks, then 6-10 more days for approved benefits to appear on utility accounts. A 48-hour shutoff notice does not guarantee expedited processing, and households remain responsible for ongoing utility payments. Sources: https://utahca.org/heat-utility-assistance/ and https://utahca.org/get-help/

contentRevisions.before:
**Eligibility Requirements**
The District of Utah U.S. Probation page says BOP staff determine eligibility for prerelease placement at contracted Residential Reentry Centers. This program is for individuals near the end of federal custody sentences or under a federal reentry plan, not for the general public. Source: https://www.utp.uscourts.gov/residential-reentry-centers-rrc

**How to Best Connect**
Eligible individuals should work with their BOP case manager, federal supervision officer, defense counsel, or reentry team. There is no independent public application for people who are not in federal custody or otherwise being placed through federal authorities.

**Access**
The District of Utah identifies The GEO Group as the contracted Bureau of Prisons halfway-house provider in Salt Lake City. The page says the facility can accommodate 95 people in-house and that placements may range from about 30 days to about one year. Residents live in a structured setting with case management, treatment coordination, job readiness training, accountability systems, 24-hour custodial care, and drug/alcohol testing.

**Important Information to Know**
This is correctional reentry housing, not emergency shelter, rental assistance, or voluntary transitional housing. Access, length of stay, and availability depend on BOP and federal supervision decisions. The current U.S. Probation page lists capacity as 95; older GEO PREA materials list different capacity figures, so confirm bed count if capacity matters. Sources: https://www.utp.uscourts.gov/residential-reentry-centers-rrc and https://www.geogroup.com/media/gygnd0zh/salt-lake-city-center-prea-certification-final-report-2021-from-t-maso-de-moya-11-8-21.pdf

**Eligibility Requirements**
OPG serves adults unable to make basic life decisions due to conditions such as aging-related illness, intellectual disabilities, brain injuries, or mental illness, often when no family or friends can care for them or abuse/neglect/exploitation is involved. Eligibility and service priority criteria apply. Source: https://daas.utah.gov/office-of-public-guardian/

**How to Best Connect**
Follow the OPG referral instructions and submit the referral form by email, mail to 288 N 1460 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84116, or fax to 801-538-8243. Call 801-538-8255 with questions.

**Access**
This is a statewide DHHS program with a Salt Lake City office. Referral is document-based rather than walk-in immediate service.

**Important Information to Know**
OPG cannot accept every referral and continues efforts to locate/reunite individuals with family or close friends when appropriate. Guardianship/conservatorship is a legal decision-making pathway; legal advice should come from a qualified attorney or court resource.

contentRevisions.before:
**Eligibility Requirements**
EHDI applies to Utah newborns and infants needing hearing screening, repeat screening, diagnostic evaluation, CMV testing after failed screening, and early intervention referral when deaf or hard of hearing. Source: https://familyhealth.utah.gov/cshcn/ehdi/

**How to Best Connect**
Parents should work with the birth facility, pediatrician, pediatric audiologist, and Utah EHDI Program. Contact Utah EHDI at 801-273-6600 when guidance is needed, especially if CMV testing timelines or follow-up are uncertain.

**Access**
Utah goals include screening before hospital discharge or before 10 days of age for out-of-hospital births, repeat screening before 10 days if failed, diagnostic hearing evaluation before 3 months after a second failed screen, CMV testing before 21 days, and early intervention enrollment before 6 months if diagnosed.

**Important Information to Know**
EHDI is a screening, follow-up, referral, and care-coordination system, not a hearing-aid payer. Time-sensitive CMV testing and pediatric audiology follow-up should not be delayed.

resources.description: FYI housing vouchers for eligible former or transitioning foster youth in Salt Lake County, administered by Housing Connect with child-welfare referrals and supportive services.
resources.hours: Housing Connect office hours not confirmed; referral access depends on public child-welfare and Housing Connect processes.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
HUD's current FYI criteria cover youth ages 18-24 who left foster care or will leave within 180 days under an eligible transition plan, and who are homeless or at risk of homelessness at age 16 or older. The FYI page identifies Notice PIH 2026-19 and warns that its older FAQ awaits updating. Source: https://www.hud.gov/hud-partners/public-indian-housing-fyi HUD states the public child-welfare agency refers eligible youth to the PHA, which then determines Housing Choice Voucher eligibility. Housing Connect announced 52 FYI vouchers for youth ages 18-24 who left or are transitioning from foster care and are homeless or at risk. Sources: https://housingconnect.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Press-Release-FYI-vouchers-2024_Redacted.pdf and https://www.hud.gov/helping-americans/housing-choice-vouchers-family

**How to Best Connect**
This is not a general open waitlist. Youth should work with DCFS/public child-welfare, youth homeless service providers, or Housing Connect agency-referral partners so the required referral can be made. Housing Connect general contact is 801-284-4400; Housing Connect’s site also has an agency-referral portal at https://housingconnect.org/connect-to-housing/.

**Access**
Housing Connect serves low- and moderate-income households in Salt Lake County. FYI vouchers provide rental assistance in the private market when a voucher is issued and leased; the 2024 award notice said vouchers were available for use beginning December 1, 2024. General Housing Connect waiting lists may be closed even when agency-referred special vouchers exist.

**Important Information to Know**
HUD describes youth vouchers as limited to 36 months, with possible extension up to 24 additional months under FSHO requirements. Voucher availability, referral sequencing, supportive-service requirements, documentation, and leasing timelines should be confirmed before relying on the program. This is rental assistance, not emergency shelter.
resources.name: Housing Connect - Foster Youth to Independence (FYI) Housing Vouchers

Men should contact Rescue Mission of Salt Lake at 801-355-1302; women should contact the Center for Women at 801-521-5925. Ask about entering or completing the New Life Program and whether transitional housing is available after graduation.

**Access**
Administrative locations are 463 S 400 W and 1165 S State Street in Salt Lake City; residential addresses for Freedom House and Hope House are not publicly listed. The homes are fully furnished, clean-and-sober, and staffed with a house manager.

**Important Information to Know**
Residents stay six to eighteen months after graduation while continuing recovery, sobriety, faith, and stability work. This is faith-based transitional housing for program graduates, not a public emergency shelter or direct rental subsidy.
resources.name: Rescue Mission of Salt Lake - Freedom House and Hope House

resources.address: 1307 S 900 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84104; drop-off at 3060 S Lester St, West Valley City, UT 84119
resources.description: HEAT utility assistance for Salt Lake and Tooele County households, including seasonal power/gas help, crisis shutoff assistance, limited water assistance, and Rocky Mountain Power HELP enrollment.
resources.hours: Utah Community Action intake line Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM; HEAT phone appointments by scheduling. Crisis shutoff callers should call 801-359-2444.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicant must be responsible for the utilities, live in Salt Lake County or Tooele County for UCA service, and have household income at or below 150% of the federal poverty level. At least one household member must be a U.S. citizen or qualified non-citizen. Required documents include USCIS legal-status documents when applicable, Social Security cards or a birth certificate for a child under 12 months, recent power and gas bills, and prior-month proof of income for all adults. UCA gives application precedence to elderly and disabled households and households with children under six; this is a priority within the broader eligible population. Source: https://utahca.org/heat-utility-assistance/

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-359-2444 to schedule a phone appointment or get application help. Applicants may apply online, email HEAT@utahca.org, mail the application to 1307 S 900 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84104, or use the drop-off location at 3060 S Lester St, West Valley City, UT 84119. For Rocky Mountain Power HELP questions, UCA also lists 844-214-3090.

**Access**
UCA's intake line is posted as Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM. HEAT assists with power and gas bills year-round and offers crisis assistance year-round for qualifying households with a qualified crisis and 48-hour shutoff notice. Seasonal assistance is once per season, October 1 through September 30. If a Rocky Mountain Power account receives a HEAT benefit, the household is automatically enrolled in HELP monthly electric-bill discounts for the next 12 months.

**Important Information to Know**
Water assistance is limited. UCA says ordinary processing can take 6-8 weeks, then 6-10 more days for approved benefits to appear on utility accounts. A 48-hour shutoff notice does not guarantee expedited processing, and households remain responsible for ongoing utility payments. Sources: https://utahca.org/heat-utility-assistance/ and https://utahca.org/get-help/
resources.name: Utah Community Action - HEAT Utility Assistance

resources.address: 500 Foothill Drive, Salt Lake City, UT 84148
resources.description: VA Salt Lake City 6-9 week residential substance-use and co-occurring mental-health treatment program for Veterans.
resources.hours: Admissions hours not posted; VA main campus services vary by program. Contact SARRTP admissions directly.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
SARRTP is for Veterans addressing substance use and co-occurring mental-health concerns, including PTSD, in a structured residential setting. The program is abstinence-based and tobacco-free; abstinence from all substances is required during the stay. VA enrollment, clinical appropriateness, and bed availability must be confirmed. Source: https://www.va.gov/salt-lake-city-health-care/programs/addiction-treatment-services/

**How to Best Connect**
Call SARRTP admissions at 801-582-1565 ext. 2706 or email SLCSARRTPAdmissions@va.gov. Veterans not already connected to VA care may need VA eligibility/enrollment screening first.

**Access**
SARRTP is based through the VA Salt Lake City Health Care System at the George E. Wahlen VA Medical Center. The VA describes a 6-9 week residential program with individual and group therapy, care coordination and case management, recreation and occupational therapy, biofeedback, optional recovery/spirituality groups, and medication management.

**Important Information to Know**
This is residential clinical treatment, not permanent housing, HUD-VASH, or a general shelter. Admission may require clinical referral and compliance with abstinence and tobacco-free rules. Availability can change with VA bed capacity.
resources.name: VA Salt Lake City Health Care - SARRTP Residential Treatment

resources.address: 437 W 200 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84101
resources.description: Emergency shelter and dining hall access point listed by Salt Lake City, with shelter access coordinated through the Homeless Connections Hotline.
resources.hours: Salt Lake City’s older winter-overflow listing described 7:00 PM-7:00 AM for seasonal overflow; current same-day access and hours must be confirmed through 801-990-9999.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Salt Lake City lists St. Vincent De Paul Shelter and Dining Hall among emergency shelters. Public pages reviewed do not publish current nightly eligibility, ID requirements, gender rules, seasonal overflow dates, or exclusion criteria. Source: https://www.slc.gov/homelessservicesdashboard-3/

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Homeless Connections Hotline at 801-990-9999 for bed availability and shelter routing before going. Salt Lake City’s dashboard identifies the hotline as the contact for shelter and assistance.

**Access**
The site is at 437 W 200 S in Salt Lake City. Salt Lake City’s housing-and-shelter page described St. Vincent de Paul as a winter overflow location with 65 beds open 7:00 PM to 7:00 AM in the 2024-25 plan; current nightly operations should be verified by hotline. Sources: https://www.slc.gov/homelessservicesdashboard-3/ and https://www.slc.gov/homelessness/housing-and-shelter/

**Important Information to Know**
This is emergency/overflow shelter access, not a guaranteed year-round bed or permanent housing placement. Capacity, operator arrangements, and seasonal hours can change; use the hotline for current same-day instructions.
resources.name: St. Vincent de Paul Shelter and Dining Hall

resources.address: 1585 W 2100 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84119
resources.description: Federal Bureau of Prisons contracted residential reentry center in Salt Lake City operated by The GEO Group for eligible people nearing release from federal custody.
resources.hours: 24-hour structured residential facility; public intake hours do not apply because placement is through BOP or federal supervision.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
The District of Utah U.S. Probation page says BOP staff determine eligibility for prerelease placement at contracted Residential Reentry Centers. This program is for individuals near the end of federal custody sentences or under a federal reentry plan, not for the general public. Source: https://www.utp.uscourts.gov/residential-reentry-centers-rrc

**How to Best Connect**
Eligible individuals should work with their BOP case manager, federal supervision officer, defense counsel, or reentry team. There is no independent public application for people who are not in federal custody or otherwise being placed through federal authorities.

**Access**
The District of Utah identifies The GEO Group as the contracted Bureau of Prisons halfway-house provider in Salt Lake City. The court page describes placements ranging from about 30 days to about one year; actual placement is decided by federal authorities. Residents live in a structured setting with case management, treatment coordination, job readiness training, accountability systems, 24-hour custodial care, and drug/alcohol testing.

**Important Information to Know**
This is correctional reentry housing, not emergency shelter, rental assistance, or voluntary transitional housing. Access, length of stay, and availability depend on BOP and federal supervision decisions. Published capacity conflicts: the U.S. Probation page lists 95, while GEO's 2026 SEC filing lists 115. Neither figure establishes available beds. Confirm placement availability with the federal reentry team. Additional source: https://investors.geogroup.com/node/18706/html Sources: https://www.utp.uscourts.gov/residential-reentry-centers-rrc and https://www.geogroup.com/media/gygnd0zh/salt-lake-city-center-prea-certification-final-report-2021-from-t-maso-de-moya-11-8-21.pdf
resources.name: The GEO Group - Salt Lake City Residential Reentry Center

resources.address: 2973 W 13800 S, Bluffdale, UT 84065
resources.description: Men's residential substance-use treatment, medical detox, and residential support homes through Renaissance Ranch, with 24/7 admissions contact.
resources.hours: Admissions available 24/7.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Renaissance Ranch describes full-service care for adult men, including medical detox, residential treatment, outpatient, and residential support homes. The site says it is now accepting Medicaid, but clinical admission criteria, insurance authorization, self-pay costs, medication policies, and bed availability must be confirmed. Source: https://www.renaissanceranch.net/

**How to Best Connect**
Call admissions at 855-736-7262 or email admissions@renaissanceranch.com. Ask specifically about Bluffdale residential treatment, detox, residential support homes, Medicaid/insurance acceptance, costs, and current openings.

**Access**
Admissions are advertised as available 24/7. The provider lists Bluffdale among its Utah locations and describes a path from detox to residential treatment to outpatient/residential support homes across Utah and Idaho.

**Important Information to Know**
This is treatment-linked housing for adult men, not general affordable housing or emergency shelter. Costs and length of stay depend on clinical placement, insurance/Medicaid or self-pay, and program availability.
resources.name: Renaissance Ranch - Men's Residential Treatment and Residential Support

resources.address: 288 N 1460 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: State disability-services pathway funding residential and in-home supports such as supported living, host homes, professional parent supports, adaptations, and support coordination through Medicaid waivers.
resources.hours: State office/intake hours not confirmed from reviewed pages; call DSPD for intake and eligibility instructions.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
DSPD services depend on which Medicaid waiver a person qualifies for. Residentially relevant services include host homes, professional parent supports, supported living, environmental adaptations, and support coordination. Formal disability eligibility, Medicaid waiver enrollment, assessment, documents, and waitlist timing must be confirmed through DSPD. Source: https://dspd.utah.gov/services/

**How to Best Connect**
Call DSPD at 801-538-4200 or toll-free 844-275-3773 to ask for intake and eligibility screening, waiver status, waiting-list information, and provider options in Salt Lake County.

**Access**
DSPD is statewide and serves eligible Utah residents, including Salt Lake County. Supported living helps people live independently in their own homes, with roommates, or with a spouse; host homes and professional parent supports can provide out-of-home placements in trained family/private-home settings.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not emergency housing and does not guarantee an apartment. Supports depend on eligibility, waiver funding, assessed need, provider capacity, and possible waiting lists. Confirm current rules before making housing plans.
resources.name: Utah DSPD - Residential Supports and Supported Living

resources.address: 3600 South Constitution Boulevard, West Valley City, UT 84119
resources.description: West Valley City homeowner repair assistance, including home rehabilitation loans, mobile home rehabilitation grants, and emergency repair grants for eligible owner-occupied properties.
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday 7:00 AM-6:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
West Valley City homeowners may qualify for home rehabilitation loans; resident owners of mobile homes may qualify for mobile home repair grants; and extremely low-income homeowners may qualify for emergency repair grants to prevent further damage. Current pages do not list all income, ownership, occupancy, property, lien, and documentation rules; use program guidelines/application links. Source: https://www.wvc-ut.gov/1365/Community-Grants-Division

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Community Grants Division at 801-963-3369, apply online through the program links, or contact the division for downloadable applications. Ask which program fits the repair and whether funds remain available.

**Access**
Applications for the 2026-2027 funding cycle opened May 1, 2026. The office is at 3600 South Constitution Boulevard in West Valley City and is open Monday through Thursday, 7:00 AM-6:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
These programs are for West Valley City properties and owner-occupants, not renters. The down-payment program listed on the same page is the Chenoa Fund loan, not a city grant. Funding, eligible repairs, loan/deferred-loan terms, and mobile-home grant terms should be confirmed before applying.
resources.name: West Valley City Community Grants Division - Home Repair Programs

resources.address: 1747 S 900 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84104
resources.description: Utah Department of Corrections residential transition and stabilization facility for male parolees, including people released from prison without approved housing.
resources.hours: 24-hour correctional residential facility; public intake hours do not apply.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Fortitude Treatment Center is designed to serve male parolees. Utah Department of Corrections says it serves as a transition facility for people released from prison who do not have appropriate housing arranged before parole, and as a stabilization facility for structured reentry planning. Source: https://corrections.utah.gov/inmate-services/reentry-and-rehabilitation/community-correctional-centers/fortitude-treatment-center/

**How to Best Connect**
Placement is through Utah Department of Corrections and Adult Probation and Parole. Eligible people should work with their institutional case manager or AP&P agent; the public cannot apply independently. Facility phone is 801-886-7800 for official program questions.

**Access**
The facility is at 1747 S 900 W in Salt Lake City. Residents are subject to stricter restrictions than ordinary community supervision and are expected to find employment, attend recommended treatment, follow center rules, and work with a case manager.

**Important Information to Know**
This is correctional reentry housing/stabilization, not a shelter, rental program, or treatment bed open to the public. Admission depends on parole status, DOC/AP&P decisions, program need, and available space.
resources.name: Utah Department of Corrections - Fortitude Treatment Center

resources.address: 850 W 1700 S, Suite 1, Salt Lake City, UT 84104
resources.description: No-cost home weatherization audits and energy-efficiency repairs for eligible households in Salt Lake, Tooele, Davis, Weber, and Morgan counties, with crisis weatherization for qualifying homeowners.
resources.hours: Utah Community Action intake line Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM; exact Weatherization office walk-in hours are not posted. Drop boxes are available outside at 850 W 1700 S, Suite 1.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Homeowners or renters may qualify when the computerized energy audit shows a clear need and household income is at or below 200% of the federal poverty level. UCA gives precedence to elderly and disabled households and households with children under age six. Required documents include Social Security cards or a HEAT approval letter, bill-history release authorization and utility bill copy, declaration and proof of ownership or owner approval, and income verification if not on HEAT. Renters need owner approval. Source: https://utahca.org/home-weatherization/

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online from UCA's Weatherization page or call 801-359-2444 for help. Completed applications and documents may be faxed to 801-214-3208, mailed to Utah Community Action Weatherization Program, 850 W 1700 S Suite 1, Salt Lake City, UT 84104, dropped in the outside drop boxes at the same address, or submitted as instructed on the application page. Weatherization email: weatherization@utahca.org.

**Access**
UCA's intake line is posted as Monday-Friday 8 AM-5 PM. The Weatherization program serves Salt Lake, Tooele, Davis, Weber, and Morgan counties. Services may include home inspection, computerized energy audit, energy education, lighting replacement, furnace/window/door repairs, carbon monoxide testing, and insulation. Crisis services are available for homeowners with no heat in winter, no air conditioning in summer, or a broken water heater; UCA says crisis applicants must be the homeowner, currently on HEAT, and the HEAT and Weatherization applications must be under the same U.S. citizen household member's name.

**Important Information to Know**
Weatherization is not a general remodel or home-rehabilitation program; painting, roof repairs, siding replacement, and most capital-value improvements are not covered. UCA says applicants should receive an approval verification letter within two weeks after a complete application, but non-crisis work may take several months or longer until the applicant reaches the top of the priority list. Sources: https://utahca.org/home-weatherization/ and https://utahca.org/get-help/
resources.name: Utah Community Action - Weatherization Assistance Program

resources.address: Mobile service in northern Utah, including Salt Lake County; no fixed public overnight shelter address posted
resources.description: Peer-run mobile Blue Bus shelter and resource access for unsheltered people in northern Utah during the coldest part of winter, with limited capacity and variable locations.
resources.hours: Seasonal winter service during the coldest part of winter; exact nightly schedule, location, and intake hours are not posted.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Nomad Alliance describes itself as serving chronically unsheltered people in Salt Lake County and northern Utah. Public pages do not post formal documentation requirements, referral requirements, or disability-access rules for sleeping on the Blue Bus. The Blue Bus page says no drug use is allowed inside or near the bus. Sources: https://www.nomadalliance.org/ and https://www.nomadalliance.org/bluebus

**How to Best Connect**
Contact Nomad Alliance before relying on the bus for a specific night because the Blue Bus is mobile and public nightly location details are not posted. Nomad Alliance's current site lists 801-688-3197 and info@nomadalliance.org; the Blue Bus page footer also lists 801-200-3573. For ordinary Salt Lake County shelter placement, also use the Homeless Connections Hotline at 801-990-9999.

**Access**
Nomad Alliance says the Blue Bus runs during the coldest part of winter and has housed 10-24 people every winter night for multiple seasons while also providing daytime supports such as water, ID vouchers, naps, phone charging, Wi-Fi, hot meals, and lockers. A January 24, 2026 Nomad Alliance media advisory says the upgraded bus includes shower and bathroom features, solar power, and interior renovations. Exact seasonal start and end dates, nightly hours, pickup/location process, ADA accessibility, and capacity for a given night are unconfirmed.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a small, grassroots, peer-run mobile shelter and resource model, not a licensed fixed-site shelter with guaranteed beds. No participant fee was found in reviewed public materials, but availability, rules, location, and accessibility must be confirmed directly each season. Sources: https://www.nomadalliance.org/bluebus and https://www.nomadalliance.org/post/media-advisory-nomad-alliance-re-launches-nation-s-first-mobile-shelter-the-upgraded-blue-bus
resources.name: Nomad Alliance - Blue Bus Mobile Shelter

resources.address: 548 S 700 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84104
resources.description: Operational non-congregate microshelter community in Salt Lake City with hard-shell pods, shared hygiene facilities, meals, and case management; referral required through coordinated shelter access.
resources.hours: Utah 211 lists service hours as 24/7 for residents; referral/placement is through the homeless services coordinated entry line, and public walk-in intake is not advertised.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Utah 211 lists the Salt Lake Microshelter Community as serving unsheltered adults, minimum age 18. It says no substance use, weapons, or alcohol are allowed on site and that a referral is required from the coordinated entry line; callers should ask for specific eligibility criteria. Source: https://utahdhhs.211utah.org/node/354752

**How to Best Connect**
Contact the Homeless Connections Hotline at 801-990-9999 for emergency shelter options and referral/placement. Shelter the Homeless says the hotline connects Salt Lake County residents experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness with emergency shelter options and community resources. Sources: https://homelessutah.org/contact-us/ and https://www.slc.gov/homelessservicesdashboard-3/

**Access**
The operational site is at 548 S 700 W in Salt Lake City. Switchpoint's page describes 50 hard-shell pods with power outlets, heating and AC, lockable doors, individualized case management, two meals per day for residents, community bathrooms and showers, and a community garden. Utah 211 lists 24/7 service hours, no cost, stays up to 120 days with possible 30-day extensions after case-management review, and couples permitted but housed in separate units. The program is often at capacity and Switchpoint notes a waiting list.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a walk-up shelter and does not guarantee an immediate pod. The Utah Office of Homeless Services says Phase II opened September 28, 2024 at the state-owned 548 S 700 W site after the pilot became a permanent program with Switchpoint; later state materials describe the site as operating 50 units, with Phase 3 expansion paused because of funding reallocations. Confirm current waitlist, pets, couple rules, accessibility, and placement route through the hotline. Sources: https://switchpoint.org/where-we-are/locations/salt-lake/microshelter, https://jobs.utah.gov/department/press/2024/093024.html, https://jobs.utah.gov/homelessness/hex.pdf, and https://le.utah.gov/interim/2026/pdf/00002346.pdf
resources.name: Switchpoint - Salt Lake Microshelter Community

resources.address: 3495 S West Temple St, South Salt Lake, UT 84115; The HUB of Opportunity, 3848 S West Temple, South Salt Lake, UT 84115
resources.description: Residential homes, supervised apartments, supported living, and Hub affordable housing connections for people with intellectual and/or physical disabilities in Salt Lake County.
resources.hours: Residential program office hours not posted on official pages; contact Columbus Community Center during business hours to confirm intake availability.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Columbus says its residential programs provide housing and support services for individuals with intellectual and/or physical disabilities. The Residential Services page says clients must first secure funding unless self-paying. Funding may come through DSPD, Vocational Rehabilitation, Medicaid, or private pay, depending on what the person qualifies for. Source: https://www.columbusserves.org/residential-services/ and https://www.columbusserves.org/funding-sources/

**How to Best Connect**
Call Columbus Community Center Residential Programs at 801-262-1552 or use the contact form on the Columbus site. Ask whether the person needs an existing DSPD budget or Medicaid waiver, whether private-pay openings exist, which residential model fits the person's support needs, current waitlists, and whether Hub apartment leasing must be handled separately through Housing Connect Property Management at 801-270-1337 or thehub@housingconnect.com. Sources: https://www.columbusserves.org/contact-us/ and https://www.columbusserves.org/

**Access**
Columbus lists residential sites at Park Creek, Foothill, Jones Court in Murray, Wren Road, The HUB in South Salt Lake, and Connor Street. Residential Homes provide family-style living and round-the-clock care for people with medical conditions or specialized support needs. Supervised Apartments support independence with structured daily-living supervision. Supported Living provides one-on-one hourly supports in a person's home. The Hub provides accessible affordable housing units and community living for individuals with disabilities. Public pages do not post office hours or vacancy status.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not emergency homeless shelter. Access depends on disability-service eligibility, funding source, provider capacity, and housing availability. Columbus notes a DSPD waiting list can apply, while immediate needs may be considered during DSPD eligibility review. Hub apartments are affordable housing, not automatically free, and property-management leasing should be confirmed separately. Sources: https://www.columbusserves.org/residential-services/, https://www.columbusserves.org/funding-sources/, and https://www.columbusserves.org/
resources.name: Columbus Community Center - Residential Services and The HUB of Opportunity

resources.address: First United Methodist Church, 203 S 200 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84111; St. Mark's Cathedral, 231 E 100 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
resources.description: Code Blue emergency winter shelter operated by Unsheltered Utah's 2nd + 2nd Coalition at downtown Salt Lake City churches on the coldest nights.
resources.hours: Only during Code Blue winter weather activations; nightly opening hours and capacity are not posted and should be confirmed before arrival.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
The program serves individuals experiencing homelessness during Code Blue weather events. Public materials reviewed did not post document requirements, ID requirements, age limits, pet policies, or exclusion rules. Salt Lake County Emergency Management says a Code Blue alert in Salt Lake County is issued when temperatures, including wind chill, are forecast to drop to 18 degrees Fahrenheit or below for two or more hours within a 24-hour period. Sources: https://unshelteredutah.org/ and https://saltlakecountyem.gov/be-prepared-community-outreach/extreme-weather/

**How to Best Connect**
For nightly activation and bed/shelter availability, call the Homeless Connections Hotline at 801-990-9999. Unsheltered Utah public materials list admin@unshelteredutah.org and info@unshelteredutah.org for organization contact, but no dedicated public shelter-intake phone was verified.

**Access**
Unsheltered Utah says it leads the 2nd + 2nd Coalition, a group of Salt Lake County nonprofits, churches, and businesses that welcomes people into emergency winter shelters or movie nights on the coldest nights. Utah Legislature 2026 materials identify the hosts as First United Methodist Church and St. Mark's Cathedral in Salt Lake City and describe warm beds, hot meals, essential supplies, and wraparound support during Code Blue events. First United Methodist Church's official site lists 203 S 200 E; St. Mark's Cathedral is at 231 E 100 S. Exact nightly hours, entry process, and capacity are variable and unconfirmed.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an emergency winter overflow/warming shelter model, not year-round housing and not guaranteed shelter every night. It operates only when activated for severe cold, and capacity can be limited. Confirm current Code Blue status and location before traveling. Sources: https://unshelteredutah.org/, https://unshelteredutah.org/our-efforts/, https://le.utah.gov/interim/2026/pdf/00002346.pdf, https://www.fumcslc.org/visit-us, and https://stmarksutah.org/
resources.name: Unsheltered Utah - 2nd + 2nd Coalition Code Blue Emergency Winter Shelter

resources.address: 80 S Orange St, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: Utah Department of Corrections women-specific community correctional center providing four-to-six-month transitional reentry housing, treatment, classes, and living-plan support for women on parole.
resources.hours: 24-hour correctional residential facility; public intake hours do not apply because placement is through Utah DOC and Adult Probation and Parole.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Utah Department of Corrections says the Orange Street Women's Center houses 60 women who are being paroled and are in a transitional phase of community re-entry. This is for women in the Utah corrections/parole system, not people seeking public emergency shelter. Source: https://corrections.utah.gov/inmate-services/reentry-and-rehabilitation/community-correctional-centers/orange-street-community-correctional-center/

**How to Best Connect**
Placement is controlled by Utah Department of Corrections and Adult Probation and Parole. Eligible women should work with their institutional case manager, parole agent, or correctional reentry team. Facility phone is 801-596-6300; Women's Treatment Resource Center phone is 801-596-6311 for official program questions.

**Access**
The facility is at 80 S Orange Street, Salt Lake City, UT 84116. UDC describes a four-month to six-month stay with gender-responsive and strength-based staff interactions. The program includes clinical treatment, cognitive/behavioral/psycho-educational classes, community involvement, pro-social activities, and planning toward a living-wage job, positive community supports, and a foundational living plan. It is a structured correctional residential program with 24-hour facility operation rather than public walk-in access.

**Important Information to Know**
This is correctional transitional housing and treatment support, not rent help, shelter, or voluntary sober living. Admission depends on parole status, DOC/AP&P placement decisions, program fit, and available space. Current public materials confirm a 60-woman capacity, but real-time availability is not posted. Source: https://corrections.utah.gov/inmate-services/reentry-and-rehabilitation/community-correctional-centers/orange-street-community-correctional-center/
resources.name: Utah Department of Corrections - Orange Street Community Correctional Center

Spy Hop serves young people through media arts programming. Use the current in-house program or specific class page to register when registration is open, or call 801-532-7500 to ask about current apprenticeships, capstone classes, and waitlists. Source: https://spyhop.org/in-house-programs/

resources.description: No-cost remote career coaching, resume help, interview preparation, mentoring, and job-search support for eligible veterans, transitioning service members, and military spouses.
resources.hours: Remote services by appointment after registration; phone/contact availability should be confirmed on the current Hire Heroes USA site.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Hire Heroes USA serves transitioning service members, veterans, and military spouses. Clients register for no-cost personalized career services and work with a career advisor; job-board and advising access depends on completing intake. Source: https://www.hireheroesusa.org/what-to-expect/

**How to Best Connect**
Register through the Hire Heroes USA job-seeker page or call 844-634-1520. After intake, ask about resume help, cover letters, interview preparation, job-search strategy, training partners, and job-board access. Source: https://www.hireheroesusa.org/what-to-expect/

**Access**
Services are national and remote, so eligible Salt Lake County residents can participate without a Utah office. Appointment timing and communication method are arranged after registration.

**Important Information to Know**
Hire Heroes USA states it is not a placement agency; it provides guidance, tools, industry connections, and one-on-one support. Employment is not guaranteed.
resources.name: Hire Heroes USA - Veteran and Military Spouse Career Services

resources.informationText:

Applicants must meet requirements for specific manufacturing, factory, warehouse, or logistics assignments. Requirements may include shift availability, experience, transportation, work authorization, and employer screening. Sources: https://www.resourcemfg.com/locations/ and https://www.prologistix.com/locations/

Search and apply through the official ResourceMFG or ProLogistix job pages, or call the Salt Lake City/West Valley branch at 801-265-1999 to confirm current openings and whether walk-ins are accepted. Sources: https://www.resourcemfg.com/jobs/ and https://www.prologistix.com/jobs/

The official location lists include Salt Lake City, Utah branches. Third-party mapping corroborates a West Valley City ResourceMFG/ProLogistix location, but suite formatting and walk-in hours should be confirmed directly before visiting.

Staffing services are generally free to applicants, but jobs change quickly and employment is not guaranteed. Confirm pay, schedule, jobsite, assignment length, background/drug-screen rules, and whether a role is temporary, temp-to-hire, or direct hire.
resources.name: Employbridge - ResourceMFG and ProLogistix West Valley Staffing

resources.description: No-cost Warriors to Work career counseling, resume and interview support, job-search tools, and employer connections for eligible Wounded Warrior Project participants and family members.
resources.hours: National remote support; contact the WWP Resource Center for current intake and appointment availability.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Warriors to Work serves registered Wounded Warrior Project warriors and eligible family support members. Family members must be registered with WWP and age 18 or older for program support. Source: https://www.woundedwarriorproject.org/programs/warriors-to-work The current Warriors to Work FAQ directs unregistered applicants to WWP registration and identifies its population as post-9/11 veterans, service members, and their families. Military affiliation alone does not establish registration eligibility. Source: https://www.woundedwarriorproject.org/programs/warriors-to-work

**How to Best Connect**
Contact the WWP Resource Center at 888-997-2586 or use the Warriors to Work page to begin registration and request career support. Source: https://www.woundedwarriorproject.org/programs/warriors-to-work

**Access**
Services are national and can be delivered by phone/online; no Salt Lake County office was verified. Appointment timing depends on WWP registration, eligibility, and staff scheduling.

**Important Information to Know**
The program includes career counseling, resume writing, interview preparation, salary negotiation tools, goal setting, military-skills translation, and networking opportunities. It is no-cost, but job placement is not guaranteed.
resources.name: Wounded Warrior Project - Warriors to Work

resources.description: State Certified Peer Support Specialist training and certification pathway for people with lived recovery experience seeking peer-support roles in Utah behavioral health settings.
resources.hours: Training cohorts and application windows vary by approved provider; contact Utah Peer Support or check the state page for current schedules.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Utah's CPSS pathway is for people who use lived experience in recovery from mental health and/or substance use disorder to support others. The Youth and Young Adult peer support track is for ages 18-30 with lived experience. Applicants must use the current online application and meet state/provider requirements. Source: https://sumh.utah.gov/education/certification/peersupportspecialists/

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Utah DHHS Office of Substance Use and Mental Health peer-support page to apply online for CPSS certification or email the Utah Peer Support Program with questions. Source: https://sumh.utah.gov/education/certification/peersupportspecialists/

**Access**
This is a statewide certification pathway. Trainings may be in person, hybrid, or virtual through approved providers, including Salt Lake-area options such as USARA in Salt Lake City, UAPSS in South Salt Lake, and Optum in Draper. Cohorts and locations change.

**Important Information to Know**
The training builds skills for peer-support work, but certification does not guarantee employment. Employers may require additional background checks, supervision, continuing education, or job-specific qualifications.
resources.name: Utah DHHS OSUMH - Certified Peer Support Specialist Training and Certification

Horizonte serves adult learners seeking English language classes, adult high school completion, GED preparation/testing, youth-to-adult programming, and CNA classes. Call 801-578-8574 or attend a posted registration session for the desired program. Ask what identification, proof of address, testing, fees, and class placement are required. Source: https://horizonte.slcschools.org/adults

Main services are at 1234 S Main St in Salt Lake City. Current pages list adult high school in-person Monday-Thursday 9:40 AM-2:00 PM and evening hybrid Monday-Thursday 4:30 PM-7:20 PM; GED Fast Track has posted in-person and online options. Schedules vary by term.

**Important Information to Know**
A Utah State Board of Education adult education directory lists Horizonte as offering ESL, ABE, ASE, GED prep/testing, and a $30 per semester fee, but current fees and waivers should be confirmed with Horizonte. This is education and credential support, not guaranteed job placement.
resources.name: Horizonte Instruction and Training Center - Adult Education

resources.hours: Training-center hours, application intake, and class schedules vary; call the Utah Training Center before visiting or applying.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants generally must meet apprenticeship requirements and obtain or pursue employment with a signatory contractor to be indentured. Sponsor-letter, document, and trade-specific requirements should be confirmed with the training center. Sources: https://www.wsctf.org/centers/utah/ and https://www.wsctf.org/apprenticeship/

**How to Best Connect**
Contact the Utah Training Center at 801-282-6535 or the local union office at 801-280-0292 to ask about applications, contractor sponsorship, pre-apprenticeship, and current openings. Source: https://www.wsctf.org/centers/utah/

**Access**
Training is based at the West Jordan Utah Training Center. Apprentices work on contractor job sites and attend related instruction; class timing and openings depend on trade and employer demand.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an earn-while-you-learn apprenticeship path, not guaranteed immediate employment. Confirm current wages, fees/dues, tools, transportation expectations, dispatch process, and sponsor requirements directly with the training center or local.
resources.name: Western States Carpenters Training Fund - Utah Apprenticeship and Pre-Apprenticeship

Use the ESLC enrollment page, email info@eslcenter.org, or call 801-328-5608 to ask about eligibility, placement, current class openings, and nearby community class locations. Source: https://www.eslcenter.org/learn

The current office is at 1270 W 2320 S, Suite F, West Valley City. The page describes practical English for daily life, work, and community, including workplace classes for job tasks and communication at work. resources.name: English Skills Learning Center - Adult and Workplace English Classes

resources.description: VA clinical vocational rehabilitation program offering Compensated Work Therapy options such as transitional work and supported employment for eligible enrolled veterans.
resources.hours: Access is by VA referral and appointment; call VA Salt Lake City or ask the veteran's VA care team for current CWT availability.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Compensated Work Therapy is a VA clinical vocational rehabilitation program for veterans with employment barriers, including physical or mental health challenges. Local participation requires VA health care access and clinical referral. Source: https://department.va.gov/vha/compensated-work-therapy/

**How to Best Connect**
An enrolled veteran should ask their VA Salt Lake City provider, mental health team, social worker, or vocational rehabilitation contact for a CWT consult. For routing, call VA Salt Lake City at 801-582-1565. Source: https://www.va.gov/salt-lake-city-health-care/contact-us/

**Access**
CWT programs are located within VA medical centers nationwide. Local access is through the George E. Wahlen VA Medical Center/VA Salt Lake City Health Care System. It is not a public walk-in job board; services depend on referral, fit, and capacity.

**Important Information to Know**
CWT may include transitional work, employment supports, and supported employment, but the reviewed local pages did not publish a direct Salt Lake CWT extension or current capacity. Participation is not a guaranteed job placement.
resources.name: VA Salt Lake City Health Care - Compensated Work Therapy

Year Up United's Salt Lake City program is designed for young adults ages 18-29. Apply through the Year Up United Salt Lake City location page. Ask about the current career track, cohort date, documents, internship rules, stipend/payment, and attendance expectations. Source: https://www.yearup.org/locations/salt-lake-city-ut

resources.name: Year Up United - Salt Lake City Career Pathways

Training is through SLTech at SLCC's Westpointe Campus. The program page lists multiple 2026 cohorts, open registration, and morning/evening-Saturday formats. Registration deadlines and class capacity should be confirmed before referral.

Call 385-414-4649 to request 55+ liaison help and ask specifically about job navigation, workforce development, computer help, and appointment times. Sources: https://sslc.gov/m/Directory and https://bear-dachshund-xs4t.squarespace.com/55-services

resources.description: Free workforce development services for Salt Lake and Tooele County adults, including CDA training, GED preparation, job readiness, financial literacy, and career-training referrals.

resources.informationText:

Utah Community Action Workforce Development serves adults age 18 and older in Salt Lake or Tooele Counties, and the page says all income levels are accepted. Program-specific requirements apply for CDA, GED preparation, job readiness, and referrals. Source: https://utahca.org/workforce-development/

Complete the online interest/application form in English or Spanish, or call the intake team at 801-359-2444. UCA states staff will follow up by phone to finish applying for the chosen program. Source: https://utahca.org/workforce-development/

Services are based through Utah Community Action in Salt Lake City, with scheduled classes and case-management meetings. CDA classes are weekly and follow a school-year schedule; GED support includes regular check-ins and online resources. ESL is referral-based rather than in-house.

resources.name: Utah Community Action - Workforce Development

resources.description: Utah state alternative application pathway allowing qualified applicants with disabilities to be considered through a noncompetitive hiring process for eligible executive-branch jobs.
resources.hours: Online application access is available through statejobs.utah.gov; ASAP review depends on each job posting and agency participation.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
ASAP is for qualified applicants with disabilities who meet minimum qualifications for eligible State of Utah executive-branch Schedule B career-service jobs. Acceptable documentation includes SSDI/SSI, VA certification, vocational rehabilitation letter, physician letter, or Schedule A letter. Source: https://dhrm.utah.gov/hiring-pathways/people-with-disabilities/

**How to Best Connect**
Apply for the state job at https://statejobs.utah.gov/, then email the recruitment number, job title, and disability documentation to asap@utah.gov. DHRM specifically says not to attach disability documentation to the job application. Source: https://dhrm.utah.gov/hiring-pathways/people-with-disabilities/

**Access**
ASAP is statewide and tied to eligible State of Utah job postings, including Salt Lake County positions when posted. Courts, legislative offices, the State Auditor, and the Attorney General are excluded. Hiring managers decide whether to use ASAP.

**Important Information to Know**
ASAP does not guarantee an interview or hire. If hired through ASAP, the applicant enters a six-month at-will on-the-job trial period before possible conversion to career service and normal probation. Documentation is kept on file for three years under current DHRM guidance.
resources.name: Utah DHRM - Alternative State Application Program

resources.description: Paid time-limited Utah state internships for qualified applicants with disabilities, posted through state jobs and coordinated through the disability hiring-pathway process.
resources.hours: Openings are posted individually on statejobs.utah.gov; schedules, duration, and benefits vary by internship posting.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Work Ability Internship positions are temporary paid internships only open to candidates with disabilities. Applicants must meet the posted qualifications and use the same documentation/hiring process as ASAP. Source: https://dhrm.utah.gov/hiring-pathways/people-with-disabilities/

**How to Best Connect**
Monitor https://statejobs.utah.gov/ for Work Ability Internship postings and follow the DHRM disability hiring-pathway instructions, including emailing documentation and the recruitment number when required. Source: https://dhrm.utah.gov/hiring-pathways/people-with-disabilities/

**Access**
This is not a standing application pool. Internships are individual state postings and may be full-time/time-limited with possible benefits, depending on the posting. Locations can include Salt Lake County or other Utah state agency sites.

**Important Information to Know**
WAI can provide work experience, education, mentoring, and skill development, but it does not guarantee permanent employment. Confirm pay, duration, benefits, location, remote/in-person requirements, and documentation steps for each posting.
resources.name: Utah DHRM and USOR - Work Ability Internship

resources.description: Free virtual career coaching, job-search training, networking, and U.S. workforce navigation for eligible immigrant, refugee, and asylee professionals in Utah and nationwide.
resources.hours: Virtual services by appointment after eligibility screening; coaching may be available for up to 12 months of a job search.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Upwardly Global serves immigrant, refugee, and asylee professionals. Current eligibility includes arriving in the U.S. within the last 10 years, having a bachelor's degree or equivalent professional training, intermediate or advanced English, work authorization, and not currently working in the professional field. Applicants may live anywhere in the U.S. Source: https://www.upwardlyglobal.org/job-seeker-resources/

**How to Best Connect**
Use Upwardly Global's job-seeker page to sign up for free expert coaching and complete eligibility screening. Source: https://www.upwardlyglobal.org/job-seeker-resources/

**Access**
Coaches can meet online, and the program is available to candidates based anywhere in the U.S. Utah is also listed among state professional-licensing guides. No Salt Lake County office was verified.

**Important Information to Know**
The program is free for those who qualify and can include resume, interview, career pathway, licensing, courses/certifications, and networking support. It does not guarantee placement and is best suited to internationally trained professionals rebuilding a professional career.
resources.name: Upwardly Global - Virtual Career Coaching for Immigrant and Refugee Professionals

**How to Best Connect**
Fill out the UCAT referral form and email it to ucat@utah.gov, or call 801-887-9380 to ask about a free consultation, device loan, custom work, or worksite assessment. Source: https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/vr/services/ucat.html

resources.description: Utah State Office of Rehabilitation Choose to Work employment specialists provide preparation and placement services for Utah job seekers with disabilities and hiring support for employers.
resources.hours: Choose to Work coordinator hours are not posted; VR intake is through local VR offices or the statewide VR line.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Choose to Work serves Utah job seekers with disabilities and employers. Job seekers generally need to qualify for Vocational Rehabilitation: a significant physical or mental impairment, a substantial impediment to employment, a need for VR services to obtain or maintain employment, and an expected employment benefit. Bring disability records if available, identification, Social Security card, and a completed VR application to a VR appointment. Sources: https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/vr/employer/choose.html and https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/vr/apply.html

**How to Best Connect**
For Choose to Work, contact Leah Lobato, Coordinator, at 801-887-9538 or leahlobato@utah.gov. Job seekers should also start through USOR Vocational Rehabilitation by calling 1-866-454-8397, contacting a local VR office, attending a welcome session, and completing a VR application. Sources: https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/vr/employer/choose.html and https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/vr/apply.html

**Access**
Choose to Work is statewide. The public Choose to Work page does not list walk-in hours or a public office for the coordinator. VR applications are handled through local VR offices, and a counselor has up to 60 days from appointment to determine eligibility unless more information is needed. Sources: https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/vr/apply.html

**Important Information to Know**
Choose to Work is no-cost and provides preparation and placement services to job seekers with disabilities while also supporting employers with recruiting, hiring, and retention. USOR VR is operating under an Order of Selection; newly eligible people in closed priority categories may be delayed and may receive only information and referral until their category opens. Sources: https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/vr/employer/choose.html and https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/vr/services/order.html
resources.name: Utah State Office of Rehabilitation - Choose to Work

resources.hours: One Utah Service Fellowship office hours are Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM; service schedules vary by host site and term.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
One Utah Service Fellowship lists eligibility for the current cohort as being in Utah, age 18 or older, having a high school diploma or GED, being a lawful U.S. citizen or green card holder, and being able to pass state and federal background checks. No prior service experience is listed as required. Source: https://www.oneutahservice.org/ousf-fall-service-cohort

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Current Openings/Start an Application page, join the waitlist if a preferred organization is not listed, or contact fellowship@oneutahservice.org. The text line is (801) 251-6654. Sources: https://www.oneutahservice.org/applicant-interest-form and https://www.oneutahservice.org/

**Access**
The program headquarters is at Utah State University - Salt Lake Center, 920 W Levoy Dr, Taylorsville. Office hours are Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM. The fellowship places members with nonprofits, government agencies, LEAs, and community organizations across Utah; host-site location, schedule, and term length vary. Sources: https://www.oneutahservice.org/ and https://www.oneutahservice.org/ousf-service-year

**Important Information to Know**
This is AmeriCorps service, not standard employment. Members receive a living allowance equivalent to at least $10/hour and a post-service education award, with training, networking, and professional-development benefits. UCC field crews are separate: the UCC official page says 2026 field crews are filled and current UCC partner individual placements are not available, so applicants should use One Utah openings for current actionable placements. Sources: https://www.oneutahservice.org/ousf-fall-service-cohort and https://www.usu.edu/ucc/positions
resources.name: One Utah Service Fellowship - Paid AmeriCorps Service Placements

resources.description: State DSBVI services for blind and visually impaired Utahns, including vocational rehabilitation, employment-readiness training, no-cost adjustment-to-blindness classes, and business-enterprise training.
resources.hours: Training and Adjustment Services classes are Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:00 PM; administrative office hours were not separately posted.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
DSBVI serves Utah residents who are blind or visually impaired. DSBVI VR serves people who are legally blind and certain qualifying people with significant visual impairments. TAS students must meet physical and mental requirements and be free from barriers that would impede attendance or progress. BEP requires legal blindness, age 18 or older, U.S. citizenship, Utah residency for at least one year, and passing an entry exam, site review, and initial interview. Sources: https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/, https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/resources/casemanagement.html, https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/training/tas.html, https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/resources/bep.html

**How to Best Connect**
Call the DSBVI Administrative Office at 801-323-4343 or 800-284-1823 if unsure which office serves you. To apply for VR, use the main USOR VR application process or drop an application at a USOR or DSBVI office. For TAS information, call Jodi Duke at 801-323-4348 or Adam Rushforth at 801-323-4347. Sources: https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/contact.html, https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/resources/casemanagement.html, https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/training/tas.html

**Access**
The Salt Lake administrative office and TAS classes are at 250 N 1950 W, Suite B, Salt Lake City. TAS classes are offered Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:00 PM and are taught at the Salt Lake site. VR services are statewide through DSBVI offices and local VR application processes. Sources: https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/contact.html and https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/training/tas.html

**Important Information to Know**
TAS is no cost to students and includes cane travel, Braille literacy, adaptive technology/computers, home management, and employment readiness. The employment specialist can help active job seekers with resumes, matching talents and skills to employment, mock interviews, and interview advocacy when the student wants it. BEP is an entrepreneurial food-service business pathway, not guaranteed wage employment. VR-funded services may be affected by USOR Order of Selection, so confirm waitlist status when applying. Sources: https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/training/tas.html, https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/resources/bep.html, https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/vr/services/order.html
resources.name: Utah Division of Services for the Blind and Visually Impaired - Training and Adjustment Services and Vocational Rehabilitation Employment

resources.address: 610 N Main St, Suite A, Clearfield, UT 84015
resources.description: USOR-approved community rehabilitation provider offering supported employment, job placement, job coaching, and customized employment services in Weber, Davis, and Salt Lake counties.
resources.hours: By appointment only; public office hours are not posted.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Beautiful Ability serves clients needing supported employment in Weber, Davis, and Salt Lake counties. USOR's approved CRP list shows Beautiful Ability as approved for Salt Lake County with supported job-based training, supported employment, customized employment, financial literacy, and supported education. Access is typically through a VR counselor or other disability-service funding pathway; confirm referral and funding requirements before intake. Sources: https://beautifulability.com/, https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/vr/partners/crpapproved.pdf, https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/vr/services/work.html

**How to Best Connect**
Call or text 801-200-2764 or email beautifulability@outlook.com. People working with USOR should ask their VR counselor whether Beautiful Ability is an appropriate CRP for job development, placement, coaching, or customized employment. Sources: https://beautifulability.com/ and https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/vr/partners/crpapproved.pdf

**Access**
The office is at 610 N Main St, Suite A, Clearfield, and the provider states it serves Weber, Davis, and Salt Lake counties. Office access is by appointment only; Salt Lake County meeting locations are not listed publicly. Job-search meetings are at least weekly while job searching, and coaching after placement is provided as needed while the person builds independence. Source: https://beautifulability.com/

**Important Information to Know**
Beautiful Ability says it matches clients to jobs they are qualified for and interested in, does not place clients in sheltered workshops or below-minimum-wage jobs, and strives for placement within 60 days after job-development activities start, though timing varies by job type and participation. Sources: https://beautifulability.com/ and https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/vr/services/work.html

resources.description: Accessible ebook library for people with qualifying print disabilities, including audio, braille-ready, and other accessible formats; free for qualified U.S. students and fee-based for many U.S. adults.
resources.hours: Online library access is available anytime; membership review and support hours are not fully posted, so confirm processing times with Bookshare.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Bookshare members must have a qualifying print disability, such as blindness/low vision, a physical impairment affecting reading or book handling, or a qualifying learning/processing impairment. Bookshare says an IEP or 504 plan is not required, but eligibility must be determined by an appropriate professional or through accepted reciprocal verification. Sources: https://www.bookshare.org/help-and-learning-articles/who-qualifies-for-bookshare and https://www.bookshare.org/who-we-are

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through Bookshare. If forms are needed, Bookshare lists membership@bookshare.org and fax 650-475-1066 for submitting sign-up materials. Start at https://www.bookshare.org/ and see sign-up guidance at https://www.bookshare.org/help-and-learning-articles/how-do-i-sign-up-for-bookshare.

**Access**
Bookshare is a national remote service available to qualified Salt Lake County residents. Members use the online library and reading tools/apps to access accessible ebooks. Online access is remote; membership processing time and support availability should be confirmed with Bookshare.

**Important Information to Know**
Bookshare says qualified U.S. students and schools are free through U.S. Department of Education/OSEP funding. U.S. adults who are not students are listed at $79.99 per year for unlimited access; discounts or partner-funded memberships may exist but are not guaranteed. Source: https://www.bookshare.org/adults
resources.name: Bookshare - Accessible Ebook Library

resources.description: No-cost IP captioned telephone and mobile captioning service for people with hearing loss who need captions to use the phone effectively.
resources.hours: CaptionCall service use is available through the phone/app; customer-care hours were not confirmed on reviewed pages.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
CaptionCall is for individuals with hearing loss that makes captions necessary to use the telephone effectively. Federal IP CTS rules restrict caption use to the registered user with hearing loss. Source: https://sorenson.com/solutions/captioning/captioncall/

**How to Best Connect**
Request CaptionCall service through Sorenson's CaptionCall page or call CaptionCall at 1-800-866-0974. Ask what self-certification, identity validation, internet/phone requirements, installation options, and mobile-app steps apply. Source: https://sorenson.com/captioncall/captioncall-home-phone/

**Access**
CaptionCall serves eligible users nationwide, including Salt Lake County residents, through a home caption phone and CaptionCall Mobile app. Service depends on internet/mobile connectivity and registration approval.

**Important Information to Know**
Sorenson states CaptionCall phone service and the mobile app are no cost to qualifying users because IP CTS is federally funded. CaptionCall materials also state the phone and app remain Sorenson property for support, service, and upgrades. Sources: https://sorenson.com/solutions/captioning/captioncall/ and https://sorenson.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/guide-captioncall-red-carpet.pdf
resources.name: CaptionCall by Sorenson - IP Captioned Telephone Service

resources.informationText:

Kauri Sue Hamilton School serves Jordan School District students ages 5-22 with significant multiple disabilities. Placement should be confirmed through the student's IEP team and Jordan District special education process; transfer/open-enrollment policies and capacity were not confirmed. Call Kauri Sue Hamilton School at 801-567-8500 and ask about special education placement procedures, IEP team referral, eligibility, transportation, and current program capacity.

**Access**
The school is in Riverton and lists Monday-Friday school hours of 8:30 AM-2:00 PM. The facility includes therapy rooms, multi-sensory spaces, a swimming pool, and specialized areas; services are school-based and not public walk-in disability services. Source: https://kaurisuehamilton.jordandistrict.org/

**Important Information to Know**
Official text describes certified special education teachers, instructional assistants, speech-language pathology, occupational and physical therapy, music therapy, nurses, behavioral specialists, adapted physical education, swimming, vocational training, home living skills, and community integration. Availability depends on district eligibility and IEP determination.
