resources.hours: Training and Adjustment Services classes are Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:00 PM; administrative office hours were not separately posted.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
DSBVI serves Utah residents who are blind or visually impaired. DSBVI VR serves people who are legally blind and certain qualifying people with significant visual impairments. TAS students must meet physical and mental requirements and be free from barriers that would impede attendance or progress. BEP requires legal blindness, age 18 or older, U.S. citizenship, Utah residency for at least one year, and passing an entry exam, site review, and initial interview. Sources: https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/, https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/resources/casemanagement.html, https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/training/tas.html, https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/resources/bep.html

**How to Best Connect**
Call the DSBVI Administrative Office at 801-323-4343 or 800-284-1823 if unsure which office serves you. To apply for VR, use the main USOR VR application process or drop an application at a USOR or DSBVI office. For TAS information, call Jodi Duke at 801-323-4348 or Adam Rushforth at 801-323-4347. Sources: https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/contact.html, https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/resources/casemanagement.html, https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/training/tas.html

**Access**
The Salt Lake administrative office and TAS classes are at 250 N 1950 W, Suite B, Salt Lake City. TAS classes are offered Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:00 PM and are taught at the Salt Lake site. VR services are statewide through DSBVI offices and local VR application processes. Sources: https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/contact.html and https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/training/tas.html

**Important Information to Know**
TAS is no cost to students and includes cane travel, Braille literacy, adaptive technology/computers, home management, and employment readiness. The employment specialist can help active job seekers with resumes, matching talents and skills to employment, mock interviews, and interview advocacy when the student wants it. BEP is an entrepreneurial food-service business pathway, not guaranteed wage employment. VR-funded services may be affected by USOR Order of Selection, so confirm waitlist status when applying. Sources: https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/training/tas.html, https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dsbvi/resources/bep.html, https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/vr/services/order.html
resources.name: Utah Division of Services for the Blind and Visually Impaired - Training and Adjustment Services and Vocational Rehabilitation Employment

**Access**
The waiver is statewide, and Salt Lake County acts as the local Area Agency on Aging access point. Services are based on assessment and can include adult day health, case management, chore, community living, emergency response, environmental accessibility adaptations, home-delivered supplemental meals, homemaker, non-medical transportation, personal attendant, respite, specialized medical equipment, and related supports.

**Important Information to Know**
The waiver serves a limited number of individuals and people can use only services they are assessed as needing. This is not emergency home care, and Medicaid eligibility, medical level-of-care, available slots, documentation, and service authorization should be confirmed before relying on coverage.
resources.name: Utah Medicaid - Aging Waiver

resources.description: Free statewide virtual helpline offering developmental screenings, parent support specialists, child-development activities, care coordination, and local referrals for Utah families with children 0-8.
resources.hours: Monday-Thursday 8:30 AM-8:30 PM; Friday 8:30 AM-5:00 PM; Saturday 10:00 AM-2:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Help Me Grow Utah is free and available to Utah pregnant parents and families with children age 8 and under. It is useful for developmental questions, screening, parenting support, and referral, but it is not a treatment provider. Source: https://helpmegrowutah.org/

**How to Best Connect**
Parents/caregivers can enroll through the Help Me Grow Utah website, call or text 801-691-5322, email helpmegrow@unitedwayuc.org, or use the provider referral link.

**Access**
Services are virtual statewide and available through text, email, phone calls, and mail in English and Spanish. Posted hours from the prior verified record are Monday-Thursday 8:30 AM-8:30 PM, Friday 8:30 AM-5:00 PM, and Saturday 10:00 AM-2:00 PM; confirm if timing is important.

**Important Information to Know**
Help Me Grow provides developmental screenings, pregnancy/postpartum screening, parenting and child-development support, activity ideas, care coordination, and referrals to local resources. Referrals depend on provider capacity and do not guarantee eligibility or appointments.
resources.name: Help Me Grow Utah

resources.address: 195 N 1950 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: Utah DHHS free 0-8 care-coordination team helping families identify needs and connect to developmental screening, early intervention, home visiting, Head Start, WIC, and related early-childhood supports.
resources.hours: General DHHS Integrated Services Program page lists Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM for the program phone; confirm 0-8 coordinator availability when calling.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
State resource pages describe 0-8 Care Coordination as free, with no eligibility requirements, for Utah parents/families with children ages 0-8. It is navigation and referral, not therapy or waiver enrollment. Sources: https://mihp.utah.gov/maternal-resource-guide-utah/childcare-and-parenting-resources and https://familyhealth.utah.gov/cshcn/integrated-services-program/

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-273-2804 or email care.coordination@utah.gov to request 0-8 Care Coordination. Ask what basic referral information is needed and whether a local health department partner or state care coordinator will follow up. Sources: https://familyhealth.utah.gov/cshcn/integrated-services-program/ and https://www.saltlakecounty.gov/health/resources/

**Access**
The program is statewide and can help Salt Lake County families by phone/email. Care coordinators assess needs, identify barriers, and connect families to developmental screenings, home visiting, early intervention, Head Start/Early Head Start, maternal and infant mental health, WIC, educational resources, providers, schools, special education staff, and community organizations.

**Important Information to Know**
Translation services are listed as available on state resource pages. This program helps with assessment, information, referral, and coordination; it does not guarantee placement in early intervention, child care, or clinical services.
resources.name: Utah DHHS - 0-8 Care Coordination

resources.description: Free online, phone, and mail learning and peer-support resources for adults adapting to vision loss, including assistive technology, safe mobility, daily living, and discussion groups.
resources.hours: Help line Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM Central; online resources are available anytime.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Hadley focuses on adults affected by vision loss, their families, and people who support them. The reviewed page does not list documentation requirements for a free account. Source: https://hadleyhelps.org/

**How to Best Connect**
Create a no-cost Hadley account online, use the Hadley Helps mobile app, call 1-800-323-4238, or email info@hadleyhelps.org for help choosing resources. Source: https://hadleyhelps.org/

**Access**
Hadley provides on-demand support online, by phone, and by mail at no cost. The help line is posted as Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM Central. Salt Lake County residents can access the program remotely.

**Important Information to Know**
Hadley offers practical learning and connection for vision-loss adjustment, including assistive technology, getting around safely, live discussions, and peer support. It is education/support, not a clinical low-vision rehabilitation provider or benefits office.
resources.name: Hadley - Vision Loss Learning and Support

resources.description: Regional Parkinson's Foundation chapter serving Utah with information, education, helpline routing, local chapter support, events, and connection to the University of Utah Movement Disorders Clinic Center of Excellence.
resources.hours: Chapter hours not posted; national Helpline availability should be confirmed when calling.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
The chapter supports people with Parkinson's disease, care partners, family members, and friends. No formal diagnosis documentation was listed for using chapter information or the helpline; clinical services through the University of Utah require separate medical scheduling and insurance/referral review. Source: https://www.parkinson.org/rockymountain

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Parkinson's Foundation Helpline at 1-800-4PD-INFO (473-4636), contact the Rocky Mountain Chapter at 720-850-8299 or RockyMountain@Parkinson.org, and use the Foundation's local resources/events tools for current Utah support groups and classes. Source: https://www.parkinson.org/rockymountain

**Access**
The Rocky Mountain Chapter serves CO, ID, MT, WY, and UT. The page identifies the University of Utah Movement Disorders Clinic as a Parkinson's Foundation Center of Excellence. Local groups, wellness classes, and events can change, so verify schedule, location, and registration before attending.

**Important Information to Know**
The Foundation provides support, information, education, and navigation; it is not itself a substitute for medical advice or emergency care. Financial assistance, class availability, and clinical appointments are limited and should be confirmed.
resources.name: Parkinson's Foundation - Rocky Mountain Chapter

resources.address: 6520 N Andrews Ave, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33309
resources.description: National Multiple Sclerosis Foundation programs offering MS-specific grants, assistive technology help, homecare/respite assistance, computer help, transportation assistance, education, support groups, and lending library resources.
resources.hours: Program application and support hours were not confirmed on reviewed pages; online program information is available anytime.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
MS Focus programs are for people affected by multiple sclerosis. Individual grants and programs have separate applications, documentation, income/funding, and availability rules that must be checked before applying. Source: https://msfocus.org/Get-Help

**How to Best Connect**
Start from the MS Focus Grants & Programs page and select the relevant program application or details. For general routing, call MS Focus at 888-673-6287. Source: https://msfocus.org/Get-Help

**Access**
Programs are national and available remotely to Salt Lake County residents when eligibility and funding allow. Listed help includes emergency assistance, healthcare assistance, homecare assistance, assistive technology, computer program, transportation assistance, support groups, events, and a lending library.

**Important Information to Know**
Assistance is not guaranteed. Program funding, waitlists, documentation, income limits, and annual terms can change. Confirm current eligibility, application windows, and whether a requested item or service is covered before relying on an award.
resources.name: MS Focus: Multiple Sclerosis Foundation - Grants and Programs

resources.address: 500 Foothill Dr, Salt Lake City, UT 84148
resources.description: Veteran Directed Care pathway connecting eligible disabled veterans in Salt Lake County with self-directed in-home care and supportive services, guided by case management through VA referral.
resources.hours: Access is by VA referral and appointment; public self-referral hours are not posted.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Salt Lake County describes Veteran Directed Care as serving disabled veterans of all ages with in-home care and supportive services that promote independent living. Eligibility details and referral must be handled through the veteran's VA primary care physician or VA social worker. Source: https://www.saltlakecounty.gov/aging-adult-services/services/home-community-based-care/

**How to Best Connect**
Ask the veteran's VA primary care physician or assigned VA social worker about referral to Veteran Directed Care. For county program context, call Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services Home & Community Based Care at 385-468-3200. Source: https://www.saltlakecounty.gov/aging-adult-services/services/home-community-based-care/

**Access**
The program is tied to VA and Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services home- and community-based care. Services are self-directed by the veteran, including hiring caregivers, with guidance from a case manager. It is not listed as a public walk-in program.

**Important Information to Know**
This is separate from Medicaid waiver services and ordinary county aging programs. VA eligibility, clinical need, budget authorization, caregiver rules, background/payroll requirements, and service availability must be confirmed through VA/county staff.
resources.name: VA Salt Lake City Health Care and Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services - Veteran Directed Care

resources.address: Intermountain Medical Center, Doty Auditorium, Building 6, 5121 Cottonwood St, Murray, UT 84107
resources.description: Community-based spinal cord injury peer-support group in Murray, affiliated with United Spinal Association, meeting monthly for connection and support.
resources.hours: Meets the 4th Saturday of every month from 5:15 PM-6:15 PM, per official group page; confirm holidays and room changes by email.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Utah Wheelhouse is described as a community-based support group for individuals with spinal cord injury. United Spinal membership is free, but the page does not state that membership is required to attend. Source: https://unitedspinal.org/group/utah-wheelhouse/

**How to Best Connect**
Email thewheelhouseutah@gmail.com before attending to confirm the meeting date, room, holiday changes, and any accessibility details. Source: https://unitedspinal.org/group/utah-wheelhouse/

**Access**
The official page lists Intermountain Medical Center, Doty Auditorium, Building 6, 5121 Cottonwood St, Murray, UT 84107. It states the group meets on the 4th Saturday of every month from 5:15 PM-6:15 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
This is peer support, not clinical rehabilitation, case management, or emergency assistance. Volunteer-led support groups can change schedule or location, so confirm before traveling.
resources.name: United Spinal Association - Utah Wheelhouse Spinal Cord Injury Peer Support

resources.description: Free one-on-one Medicare counseling and assistance for Utah Medicare beneficiaries, including people under 65 who qualify for Medicare by disability.
resources.hours: Counseling is by local SHIP availability; statewide phone hours were not posted on reviewed pages.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
SHIP serves people needing Medicare counseling and assistance. This includes Medicare beneficiaries and people approaching Medicare eligibility, including adults under 65 who receive Medicare because of disability. Source: https://www.shiphelp.org/ships/utah/

**How to Best Connect**
Call Utah SHIP at 1-800-541-7735 or use the SHIP locator/local Utah SHIP website to request a counselor in Salt Lake County. Source: https://www.shiphelp.org/ships/utah/

**Access**
Utah SHIP provides statewide local Medicare counseling. Counselor locations and appointment availability vary by county and season, especially around Medicare open enrollment.

**Important Information to Know**
SHIP provides counseling and application assistance, not direct financial aid or legal representation. Confirm local appointment availability and bring Medicare, insurance, prescription, income/asset, and notice documents relevant to the question.
resources.name: Utah SHIP - Senior Health Insurance Information Program

resources.address: 6715 S 1300 E, Suite 250, Salt Lake City, UT 84121
resources.description: Utah vision-access nonprofit providing child and adult vision screenings, community vision clinics, free eye exams and prescription glasses assistance for eligible patients, replacement-glasses help, and SightFest clinics.
resources.hours: Clinic and event hours vary; office hours were not posted on the reviewed page. Apply or call before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Friends for Sight says its community clinics provide an avenue for free eye exams and prescription glasses for eligible children and adults. Exact income, insurance, school, prescription, and documentation requirements should be confirmed through the application. Source: https://friendsforsight.org/programs

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Eye Exams and Glasses application link on the Friends for Sight programs page, call 801-524-2020 or 1-800-675-LOOK, or ask about upcoming screenings/SightFest events. Source: https://friendsforsight.org/programs

**Access**
Friends for Sight lists clinics at Glendale-Mountain View Community Learning Center, Liberty Community Learning Center, and Parkview Elementary School, plus SightFest events across Utah. Event and appointment times vary and are not walk-in unless advertised.

**Important Information to Know**
The program can help with free exams, prescription glasses, replacement glasses with a valid prescription, and referrals for advanced care when needed. Funding, appointments, eligibility, and provider availability are limited and should be confirmed before relying on assistance.
resources.name: Friends for Sight - Vision Clinics and Eye Exams/Glasses Assistance

resources.address: 195 N 1950 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: Utah Medicaid HCBS Community Supports Waiver for people with intellectual disabilities or related conditions, with assessed supports such as personal assistance, respite, supported living, residential habilitation, employment supports, and environmental adaptations.
resources.hours: State waiver office hours not posted; call DSPD for intake and eligibility instructions.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
The Community Supports Waiver requires functional impairment in three or more major life areas, qualifying onset before age 18 for intellectual disability or before age 22 for related conditions, primary condition not attributable to mental illness, ICF/ID level of care, Medicaid financial eligibility, ability to live safely in the community, and no age restriction. The waiver has a waiting list. Source: https://medicaid.utah.gov/ltc-2/cs/

**How to Best Connect**
Call Utah DSPD at 801-538-4200 to ask about intake, eligibility, waiting list, Medicaid waiver screening, support coordination, and Salt Lake County provider options. Source: https://medicaid.utah.gov/ltc-2/cs/

**Access**
The waiver is statewide, including Salt Lake County. Services are authorized only as assessed and may include behavioral consultation, day supports, environmental adaptations, personal assistance, respite, residential habilitation, specialized medical equipment, supported employment, supported living, and waiver support coordination. DSPD's Self-Administered Services model may let eligible people/families hire, train, and supervise in-home support employees with a required fiscal agent. Source: https://dspd.utah.gov/services/service-delivery/

**Important Information to Know**
Enrollment is limited and the waiting list can be significant. Self-Administered Services is not a standalone intake route; it is a service-delivery model for eligible DSPD services and requires a fiscal agent for payroll, background checks, and budget support. Confirm current waitlist status, Medicaid eligibility, assessment, documentation, and whether services can be self-administered.
resources.name: Utah Medicaid and DSPD - Community Supports Waiver

resources.address: 1721 Campus Center Dr, Salt Lake City, UT 84112
resources.description: University of Utah Tanner Dance disability programs including LEADD adult arts education, Elevate Theatre Company, adaptive needs dance classes, wheels dance, and related art/performance classes.
resources.hours: Class schedules vary by program; examples include LEADD Monday-Thursday 12:30 PM-3:30 PM, Elevate Saturdays 9:00 AM-11:30 AM, and adaptive dance classes on posted weekday/Saturday times.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Programs serve dancers with disabilities. LEADD is for adults with physical and/or intellectual disabilities who have aged out of the public school system; Elevate is for performers with disabilities; adaptive needs dance classes are for children and young adults with disabilities. LEADD and Elevate require a meeting/interview before registration. Source: https://tannerdance.utah.edu/dancers-with-disabilities/

**How to Best Connect**
For LEADD and Elevate, email Ben Tillotson at ben.tillotson@utah.edu to schedule a meeting before registration. For DSPD billing, Tanner Dance instructs families not to register online and to contact Sarah Cardenas at s.cardenas@utah.edu with the support coordinator's name, phone, and email. Source: https://tannerdance.utah.edu/dancers-with-disabilities/

**Access**
Programs are held at the University of Utah Tanner Dance site in Salt Lake City. Posted examples for 2026-2027 include LEADD classes Monday-Thursday 12:30 PM-3:30 PM, Elevate Theatre Company Saturdays 9:00 AM-11:30 AM, and adaptive dance/art classes at posted weekday or Saturday times.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a free program. The 2026-2027 catalog lists many LEADD/Elevate classes at $1,224 and adaptive dance classes around $710-$730, with a lower-cost InteGreat session listed separately. Scholarships and DSPD billing may help but are not guaranteed; parking, class fit, support needs, and registration availability should be confirmed.
resources.name: University of Utah Tanner Dance - Dancers with Disabilities Programs

resources.description: Long-Term Care Ombudsman advocacy contact for Salt Lake County residents of nursing homes, assisted living, and other covered long-term care facilities.
resources.hours: Ombudsman line hours were not posted on the reviewed page; call and leave a message if needed.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
The Ombudsman program helps with concerns involving long-term care facility residents. The Salt Lake contact is county-based; people should use the county where the facility/resident is located. Source: https://daas.utah.gov/ombudsman-locations-3/

**How to Best Connect**
For Salt Lake County, call the Ombudsman Line at 385-468-3255 or email ombudsman@slco.org. If concerns are not addressed or further help is needed, the state ombudsman contact is listed on the DHHS locations page. Source: https://daas.utah.gov/ombudsman-locations-3/

**Access**
The Salt Lake Ombudsman serves Salt Lake County facilities. Hours and response times were not posted, so callers should leave clear contact information, facility name, resident concern, and urgency if voicemail is reached.

**Important Information to Know**
This is rights advocacy and complaint help for facility residents, not emergency response, independent-living case management, or legal representation. For immediate danger, use emergency or protective-service channels.
resources.name: Utah Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program - Salt Lake County

resources.address: 195 N 1950 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: Utah Medicaid HCBS Community Transitions Waiver helping people with intellectual disabilities or related conditions transition from ICF settings into community living with assessed supports.
resources.hours: State waiver office hours not posted; contact the transition program manager or DSPD/Medicaid for current referral steps.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
The Community Transitions Waiver requires ICF level of care, qualifying onset before age 18 for intellectual disability or before age 22 for related conditions, functional impairment in three or more major life areas, and Medicaid financial eligibility. It is designed for transition out of an Intermediate Care Facility for people with intellectual disabilities into community settings. Source: https://medicaid.utah.gov/ltc-2/community-transitions-home/

**How to Best Connect**
Contact the listed Transition Program Manager, Glen Larsen, at 385-303-8593 or glenlarsen@utah.gov, and ask about eligibility, referral, ICF transition planning, Medicaid requirements, and available waiver capacity. Source: https://medicaid.utah.gov/ltc-2/community-transitions-home/

**Access**
The waiver is statewide, including Salt Lake County. Services are limited to assessed needs and can include behavioral consultation, community transition services, day supports, environmental adaptations, extended living supports, homemaker, nursing, personal assistance, residential habilitation, respite, supported employment, supported living, and waiver support coordination. DSPD's Self-Administered Services model may be an option for eligible in-home supports when a fiscal agent is used. Source: https://dspd.utah.gov/services/service-delivery/

**Important Information to Know**
The number served depends on funding, and services are not automatic. Self-Administered Services is not a separate public program for people who are not waiver eligible; it is a way eligible people/families can hire and supervise some supports with fiscal-agent payroll/background-check help. Confirm current slots, facility-transition eligibility, and service-delivery options.
resources.name: Utah Medicaid and DSPD - Community Transitions Waiver

resources.address: North Salt Lake campus: 665 N Cutler Dr, North Salt Lake, UT 84054; district office listed at 1948 W 2425 S, Woods Cross, UT 84087
resources.description: Utah public charter school for students with autism and other neurodiversities, offering small classes, individualized instruction, social-skills curriculum, behavioral supports, and related school services.
resources.hours: School and office schedules vary by campus/calendar; call before visiting. Public website did not show a single enrollment office hour schedule in reviewed text.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Spectrum Academy describes itself as a Utah charter school for students with autism and other neurodiversities who would benefit from its learning environment. Charter enrollment/lottery requirements, grade availability, diagnosis/IEP expectations, and deadlines should be confirmed through the school's enrollment page. Source: https://www.spectrumcharter.org/

**How to Best Connect**
Use Spectrum Academy's enrollment page or call the main number, 801-936-0318, to ask about campus options, lottery/deadlines, waitlists, transportation, IEP/504 services, and whether a diagnosis is required for the current admissions cycle. Source: https://www.spectrumcharter.org/

**Access**
Spectrum Academy lists North Salt Lake and Pleasant Grove campuses and says it serves students from across Utah's Wasatch Front. Campuses are outside Salt Lake County, so families should confirm transportation, commute feasibility, and campus assignment.

**Important Information to Know**
The school is tuition-free as a public charter, but admission is not guaranteed and depends on charter enrollment rules and available seats. Related services and accommodations depend on school evaluation and student plans; verify current program fit before leaving an existing placement.
resources.name: Spectrum Academy - Neurodiverse Public Charter School

resources.address: Craig H. Neilsen Rehabilitation Hospital / University of Utah Health, Salt Lake City, UT; Sugar House therapy access commonly listed at 1280 E Stringham Ave, Salt Lake City, UT 84106
resources.description: University of Utah Health interdisciplinary amputee rehabilitation and prosthetics program offering medical rehabilitation, therapy, prosthetic fitting/training, pain management, counseling, education, and community-resource information.
resources.hours: Clinical visits are by appointment/referral; public page does not post clinic hours.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
The program treats people with limb loss or limb difference, including leg, foot, finger, hand, arm, and multiple-limb amputations. Clinical eligibility, referral requirements, insurance authorization, and appointment availability must be confirmed with University of Utah Health. Source: https://healthcare.utah.edu/neilsen-physical-rehab-hospital/specialties/amputee

**How to Best Connect**
Use the University of Utah Health patient referral/contact path or call 801-646-8000 to ask about amputee program scheduling. For therapy-service routing, the submitted Salt Lake contact was 801-581-2221; confirm the correct clinic before going.

**Access**
Services are local to University of Utah Health/Craig H. Neilsen Rehabilitation Hospital and related therapy sites. Appointments are scheduled; this is not a drop-in support group or equipment giveaway.

**Important Information to Know**
The program includes rehabilitation physicians, physical and occupational therapists, prosthetists, surgeons, nurses, social workers, rehabilitation psychologists, prosthetic limb fitting, pain management, and education. Costs depend on insurance and clinical authorization. Any monthly amputee support group date/location should be confirmed separately before attending.
resources.name: University of Utah Health - Amputee Program

resources.address: University of Utah Clinical Neurosciences Center, 175 N Medical Dr E, Salt Lake City, UT 84132
resources.description: Huntington's Disease Society of America Utah Chapter support, education, social-work/resource navigation, support groups, and connection to University of Utah HD specialty care.
resources.hours: Chapter and support-group schedules vary; national helpline and clinic appointment hours should be confirmed when calling.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
HDSA Utah Chapter resources are for people and families impacted by Huntington's disease, including loved ones and at-risk relatives. Clinic eligibility, genetic testing, referral, and insurance requirements must be handled through medical providers. Source: https://utah.hdsa.org/

**How to Best Connect**
Use the HDSA Utah Chapter website to find current events and support groups, call the HDSA helpline at 800-345-HDSA (4372), or use HDSA's resource locator. For University of Utah clinic care, call the clinic contact directly and confirm referral/insurance needs. Source: https://utah.hdsa.org/

**Access**
The Utah Chapter posts Salt Lake City events and identifies HDSA support groups as free for individuals, loved ones, and families impacted by HD. The chapter also references the University of Utah as an HDSA Center of Excellence. Group dates and locations can change.

**Important Information to Know**
HDSA chapter support and social-worker/resource information do not replace medical, legal, or genetic counseling. Confirm current support-group schedule, clinic referral requirements, and privacy considerations before sharing genetic or health information.
resources.name: HDSA Utah Chapter and University of Utah HD Care Pathway

resources.address: Program administration: 1800 15th St, Suite 100, Denver, CO 80202; treatment is through volunteer Utah dentists
resources.description: Donated Dental Services program providing donated comprehensive dental treatment through volunteer dentists for eligible Utah applicants who cannot afford care and are 65+, permanently disabled, or need medically necessary dental care.
resources.hours: Application access is online/mail; coordinator hours were not posted on the reviewed page.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Applicants must have no means to afford dental care and meet one criterion: over age 65, permanently disabled, or need medically necessary dental care. The program does not provide emergency or cosmetic treatment. Source: https://dentallifeline.org/utah/

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through the Utah DDS page, download/mail an application, upload additional documents as requested, or contact Utah DLN Coordinator Brandon Leviton at 801-499-6504 or bleviton@DentalLifeline.org. Source: https://dentallifeline.org/utah/

**Access**
Dental Lifeline Network lists all Utah counties as open to new applications. Treatment is provided by volunteer Utah dentists when an applicant is accepted and matched; the administrative office is in Denver.

**Important Information to Know**
The program is not emergency dental care and not every applicant is accepted. Wait times can be long, documentation may be required, and medically necessary cases/veteran instructions may have special application rules. Confirm current county status and expected wait before relying on treatment.
resources.name: Dental Lifeline Network Utah - Donated Dental Services

resources.address: USDB Salt Lake campus: 1655 E 3300 S, Millcreek, UT 84106
resources.description: Statewide USDB Parent Infant Program providing birth-to-3 home-based early intervention and family coaching for deaf/hard-of-hearing and blind/visually impaired children through Baby Watch collaboration.
resources.hours: Home visits and groups are scheduled by IFSP/individual need; office hours were not confirmed.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
USDB's hearing PIP services are for deaf and hard-of-hearing children, with eligibility determined through a hearing diagnosis. The program works with Utah Baby Watch Early Intervention. USDB also documents a Parent Infant Program for blind and visually impaired infants/toddlers, with family coaching and vision-skill support. USDB directs infant/toddler referrals through Baby Watch; ask for the hearing or vision team appropriate to the child. Sources: https://www.usdb.org/parents and https://sites.google.com/usdb.org/parentinfantprogramfortheblind/home Sources: https://www.usdb.org/deaf-school/early-childhoodbirth-to-age-3 and https://familyhealth.utah.gov/oec/early-childhood-utah-resources/

**How to Best Connect**
For Salt Lake County Baby Watch routing, contact USDB Parent Infant Programs at 801-629-4749 or 801-629-4743, or work through local Baby Watch providers listed for Salt Lake County. Source: https://familyhealth.utah.gov/oec/early-childhood-utah-resources/

**Access**
PIP services are offered throughout Utah. USDB says PIP specialists are members of each Early Intervention team, visits are home-based in natural settings, and frequency is based on the child's IFSP and individual needs. Source: https://www.usdb.org/deaf-school/early-childhoodbirth-to-age-3

**Important Information to Know**
USDB says Deaf and Hard of Hearing services through USDB are free and include ASL and Listening and Spoken Language options, PIP groups, ASL resources, statewide activities, and story time. Confirm referral steps, diagnosis documentation, and whether the hearing or vision PIP team is the correct route.
resources.name: Utah Schools for the Deaf and the Blind - Parent Infant Program

resources.address: 5296 S Commerce Dr, Suite 305, Murray, UT 84107
resources.description: Statewide disability self-advocacy group by and for people with disabilities, offering peer education, leadership development, and community advocacy opportunities.
resources.hours: Meeting times and local chapter schedules are not posted on the reviewed page; contact UDDC to confirm current Salt Lake opportunities.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
People First of Utah is a self-advocacy group by people with disabilities for people with disabilities. The page does not list formal documentation requirements to get involved. Source: https://uddc.utah.gov/get-involved/training-and-education/people-first-of-utah/

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-245-7350 or email mcaldwell@utah.gov to ask about current People First groups, Salt Lake County meetings, accessibility, and how to participate. Source: https://uddc.utah.gov/get-involved/training-and-education/people-first-of-utah/

**Access**
People First is statewide through the Utah Developmental Disabilities Council. Meeting locations, virtual options, and schedules must be confirmed because the public page does not list current local times.

**Important Information to Know**
This is self-advocacy, leadership, and peer education. It is not case management, personal care, benefits enrollment, legal representation, or emergency support.
resources.name: Utah Developmental Disabilities Council - People First of Utah

resources.address: 3269 S Main St, #230, Salt Lake City, UT 84115
resources.description: Free statewide mental illness peer support, family support groups, education classes, resources, advocacy, and helpline-style information for individuals, families, and caregivers.
resources.hours: Support-group and class schedules vary; office/help availability should be confirmed by phone or email.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
NAMI Utah serves individuals living with mental illness and their families/caregivers. Public pages do not list diagnosis documentation requirements for support groups or education resources. Source: https://namiut.org/

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-323-9900, email information@namiut.org, or use the NAMI Utah support group, education, and HelpLine/resource links to find current groups and classes. Source: https://namiut.org/

**Access**
NAMI Utah lists support groups, classes, and resources throughout Utah, with a Salt Lake City office. Group locations, virtual options, registration, and schedules change and should be confirmed before attending.

**Important Information to Know**
NAMI is not a clinical treatment provider and is not a crisis provider. The site directs anyone struggling or in crisis to call/text 988 or chat 988lifeline.org. Peer support and education can complement, but not replace, professional care.
resources.name: NAMI Utah - Peer Support, Family Support, and Education

resources.address: Southwest Regional Center, Oceanside, CA; serves Utah applicants through the Southwest region
resources.description: National nonprofit placing trained service dogs, hearing/task assistance, skilled companions, facility dogs, medical alert dogs, and veteran service dogs at no cost to qualified recipients, with Utah served by the Southwest region.
resources.hours: Application and team-training schedules vary; regional office hours were not confirmed on reviewed pages.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Canine Companions places dogs with adults and children with disabilities, facility professionals serving clients with special needs, veterans with disabilities including PTSD-related tasks, and certain medical-alert needs. Hearing dogs are an additional pathway for Deaf or hard-of-hearing adults, with sound-alert tasks; ask which regional center manages this specific program. Applicants must meet program-specific eligibility, care, travel/training, and matching requirements. Source: https://canine.org/service-dogs/our-dogs/hearing-dogs/ Source: https://canine.org/service-dogs/our-dogs/

**How to Best Connect**
Start with Canine Companions' application information on its official site or call 1-800-572-2275. Utah applicants should ask which regional center handles them, current wait times, required travel, documentation, and whether their disability-related tasks match a Canine Companions dog. Source: https://canine.org/service-dogs/our-dogs/

**Access**
Canine Companions serves nationally through regional training centers; Utah is served through the Southwest region. Applicants generally must complete a multi-step application and, if matched, attend team training at the assigned regional center.

**Important Information to Know**
Dogs are provided at no cost, but acceptance and matching are not guaranteed, wait times can be long, and recipients are responsible for ongoing dog care and program requirements. Confirm current regional process, travel/lodging expectations, and whether the organization trains for the needed tasks.
resources.name: Canine Companions - Service Dogs and Assistance Dogs

resources.address: 25 Massachusetts Ave NW, Suite 650, Washington, DC 20001
resources.description: National limb loss and limb difference support services, including Certified Peer Visitor connections, healthcare navigation, support-group network help, information specialists, National Limb Loss Resource Center resources, and education.
resources.hours: Office hours Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM Eastern, per contact page.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Amputee Coalition support services are for people with limb loss or limb difference, family members, caregivers, and professionals seeking information/support. The reviewed pages do not list proof-of-disability requirements for general navigation or peer support. Sources: https://amputee-coalition.org/service/find-support-services/ and https://amputee-coalition.org/contact-us/

**How to Best Connect**
Call 888-267-5669, use the online Get Assistance/contact form, email peersupport@amputee-coalition.org for Certified Peer Visitors, email supportgroup@amputee-coalition.org for support-group network help, or connect with a Healthcare Navigator through the support-services page. Sources: https://amputee-coalition.org/contact-us/ and https://amputee-coalition.org/service/find-support-services/

**Access**
Services are national and remote, available to Salt Lake County residents. The contact page lists office hours as Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM Eastern. Virtual groups and peer visits may require registration and depend on volunteer availability.

**Important Information to Know**
Healthcare Navigators can help with insurance coverage/appeals, communicating with care teams, prosthetic/orthotic/DME understanding, local resources, and accessibility accommodations. This is information and peer/navigation support, not medical advice, legal representation, or guaranteed financial assistance.
resources.name: Amputee Coalition - Support Services and National Limb Loss Resource Center

resources.address: 7501 S 1000 E, Midvale, UT 84047
resources.description: Canyons School District special education school offering individualized instruction and related services to maximize independence, communication, self-advocacy, and community participation for students with significant disabilities.
resources.hours: Office hours Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM; early childhood sessions listed as AM 8:20 AM-10:50 AM and PM 11:30 AM-2:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Jordan Valley School serves Canyons District students placed through special education/IEP processes. Current public pages describe individualized instruction and related services; exact age range, disability criteria, transfer rules, and capacity should be confirmed with Canyons District. Source: https://jordanvalley.canyonsdistrict.org/about-us/

**How to Best Connect**
Call Jordan Valley School at 801-826-7200 and ask about special education placement, IEP team referral, early childhood contact, transportation, and current program capacity. For early childhood, the page lists 801-826-5112. Sources: https://jordanvalley.canyonsdistrict.org/ and https://jordanvalley.canyonsdistrict.org/early-childhood/

**Access**
The school is in Midvale. Office hours are Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-4:30 PM. Early childhood sessions are listed as AM 8:20 AM-10:50 AM and PM 11:30 AM-2:00 PM. Source: https://jordanvalley.canyonsdistrict.org/

**Important Information to Know**
This is a school placement, not a public drop-in disability center. Admission and services depend on district residency/placement rules, IEP team decisions, evaluations, staffing, and capacity.
resources.name: Canyons School District - Jordan Valley School

resources.address: 417 Wakara Way, Suite 1112, Salt Lake City, UT 84108
resources.description: University of Utah Health outpatient speech-language-hearing clinic providing audiology evaluation/treatment, hearing aids/cochlear implant services, speech-language evaluations and therapy, AAC, aural rehabilitation, voice, stuttering, aphasia, and Parkinson's speech therapy.
resources.hours: Appointments are scheduled; clinic hours were not posted on the reviewed page.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
The clinic serves children and adults with hearing, speech, language, developmental, and acquired neurological communication disorders. It treats people with developmental disabilities such as autism, Down syndrome, and cerebral palsy, and neurological disorders such as aphasia, traumatic brain injury, ALS, Parkinson's disease, and Alzheimer's disease. Source: https://healthcare.utah.edu/speech-language-hearing-clinic

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-581-3506 to schedule. For audiology services email hearing@utah.edu; for speech-language services email speechpath@utah.edu. Source: https://healthcare.utah.edu/speech-language-hearing-clinic

**Access**
The clinic is an outpatient University of Utah Health clinic serving the greater Salt Lake City community. Services are by appointment. The clinic also serves as a graduate training program; services are provided by graduate student clinicians under direct supervision of licensed clinical faculty providers.

**Important Information to Know**
Fees, insurance acceptance, sliding-scale options, and wait times were not confirmed on the reviewed page. The clinic provides evaluation and treatment, not school IEP placement or emergency care. Ask about costs, referrals, telehealth, and expected clinician model when scheduling.
resources.name: University of Utah Health - Speech-Language-Hearing Clinic

resources.address: Adult clinic: 175 N. Medical Drive East, 4th Floor, Salt Lake City, UT 84132; pediatric clinic: 81 N. Mario Capecchi Dr., Floor 3, Salt Lake City, UT 84112
resources.description: MDA Care Center pathway at University of Utah Health for adults and children with muscular dystrophy, ALS, spinal muscular atrophy, Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, and other neuromuscular disorders.
resources.hours: Clinical Neurosciences Center location posts Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; pediatric clinic hours were not confirmed.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
People with suspected or diagnosed neuromuscular disorders may seek MDA Care Center services; University of Utah states the clinic treats adults and children with 40+ neuromuscular disorders. Referral, insurance, and appointment availability should be confirmed with the clinic. Sources: https://www.mda.org/care/mda-care-centers and https://healthcare.utah.edu/neurosciences/neurology/muscular-dystrophy-clinic

**How to Best Connect**
Call the adult University of Utah muscular dystrophy clinic at 801-585-7575. For pediatric MDA care listed by MDA, call 801-587-0462. MDA also offers Resource Center support through https://www.mda.org/care/mda-resource-center.

**Access**
Adult care is listed at the Clinical Neurosciences Center, 175 N. Medical Drive East, 4th Floor, Salt Lake City; that location posts Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM. Pediatric care is listed by MDA at 81 N. Mario Capecchi Dr., Floor 3, Salt Lake City. Confirm referral requirements, clinic schedule, and insurance before relying on a visit.

**Important Information to Know**
MDA Care Centers provide multidisciplinary neuromuscular care and connection to MDA/community resources, not guaranteed financial coverage. Costs, insurance acceptance, wait times, and clinical-trial availability vary by patient and clinic.
resources.name: MDA and University of Utah Health - MDA Care Centers

resources.description: No-cost MDA Summer Camp for eligible youth with neuromuscular disease, with in-person and virtual sessions offered seasonally.
resources.hours: Seasonal camp sessions; application windows and session schedules vary by year.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
MDA Summer Camp is for children and young adults ages 8-17 diagnosed with a neuromuscular disease. Campers may participate in one session each year, selecting an in-person or virtual session that fits their needs. Source: https://www.mda.org/summer-camp

**How to Best Connect**
Use the Camper Information and in-person/virtual camp links on the MDA Summer Camp page, or contact MDA's Resource Center through https://www.mda.org/care/mda-resource-center for help navigating registration.

**Access**
Camp is seasonal. MDA states both in-person and virtual sessions are available each summer, but locations, dates, deadlines, and space vary. Utah families may need to travel for an in-person regional session.

**Important Information to Know**
MDA states camp is provided at no cost to families. Camp includes volunteer health professionals and trained camp volunteers, but acceptance is not guaranteed and medical needs must be reviewed through the camp process.
resources.name: Muscular Dystrophy Association - MDA Summer Camp

resources.address: 1050 W 500 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84104
resources.description: Licensed adult day services with activities, meals, caregiver respite, and transportation options for adults 18+ with disabilities, dementia, cognitive impairments, chronic conditions, or aging-related needs.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday daytime program; exact daily program hours should be confirmed with Neighborhood House.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Neighborhood House serves adults age 18 and older, including people with developmental disabilities, dementia, cognitive impairments, physical disabilities, chronic conditions, or aging-related support needs. Enrollment capacity, funding, and care fit must be confirmed directly. Source: https://www.nhutah.org/services/adult-day-care

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-363-4589 or use Neighborhood House's adult day care contact route to ask about enrollment, assessment, transportation, fees, and funding options.

**Access**
Services are provided at 1050 W 500 S in Salt Lake City. The program offers daytime support on weekdays and states that door-to-door transportation may be available within service boundaries for a separate fee; confirm current transportation area and schedule.

**Important Information to Know**
The program is not universally free. Neighborhood House describes a sliding fee scale and separate transportation fee. Confirm whether Medicaid, DSPD, private pay, or other funding is accepted for the specific participant.
resources.name: Neighborhood House - Larry H. and Gail Miller Family Foundation Adult Day Services

resources.address: 5709 S 1500 W, Taylorsville, UT 84123
resources.description: State DSDHH employment services and job-seeker resources for Deaf, Hard of Hearing, and DeafBlind Utahns, plus employer barrier-resolution and Deaf-awareness support.
resources.hours: Sanderson Center hours were not confirmed on the employment page; contact the front desk before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
DSDHH serves Deaf, Hard of Hearing, and DeafBlind Utahns and their families. The employment page provides job-seeker and employer resources; individual eligibility for direct staff help should be confirmed with DSDHH. Sources: https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dhh/ and https://jobs.utah.gov/usor/dhh/programs/employment.html

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Sanderson Center front desk at 801-263-4860 voice, 801-657-5200 VP, text 385-414-5677, or call the listed employment contact Pamela Mower at 801-657-5223.

**Access**
Services are based at the Sanderson Community Center, 5709 S 1500 W, Taylorsville. Current DSDHH pages list support, training, resources for job seekers, employer education, and barrier-resolution assistance. Confirm whether an appointment is needed.

**Important Information to Know**
The public page does not publish a full application checklist. It includes resource materials and a staff contact, so applicants should confirm what documentation, VR referral, or appointment steps are needed for one-to-one employment support.
resources.name: Utah Division of Services of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing - Employment Services

resources.address: 5296 S Commerce Drive, Suite 302, Murray, UT 84107
resources.description: Free statewide Parent Training and Information Center support, consultation, and training for families of children and youth with disabilities navigating special education, 504 plans, transition, and disability systems.
resources.hours: Phone/email support Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM; in-person office Monday-Thursday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
The PTI Project supports Utah families of children and young adults with disabilities, plus educators and service providers. It focuses on special education, disability services, rights, advocacy skills, and family-professional partnerships. Sources: https://utahparentcenter.org/program/pti/ and https://utahparentcenter.org/contact-us/

**How to Best Connect**
Call 801-272-1051 or 800-468-1160, email info@utahparentcenter.org, or use the Utah Parent Center contact form to connect with a parent consultant or training.

**Access**
Support is statewide and provided primarily by phone, email, trainings, and workshops; in-person office access is at 5296 S Commerce Drive, Suite 302, Murray. Posted phone/email hours are Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM, and in-person office hours are Monday-Thursday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM.

**Important Information to Know**
Services are free and confidential, but PTI is navigation, training, and advocacy support; it does not itself provide therapy, personal care, school placement, Medicaid eligibility, or legal representation.
resources.name: Utah Parent Center - Parent Training and Information Project

resources.address: 195 N 1950 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: Utah Medicaid HCBS Physical Disabilities Waiver for eligible adults with significant physical disabilities who need personal assistance to remain in home or community settings.
resources.hours: State office hours were not confirmed; call DSPD for current intake hours.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Utah Medicaid states the Physical Disabilities Waiver is for adults 18+ with physician-certified physical disability, functional loss of two or more limbs, at least 14 hours per week of personal assistance need, ability to direct attendants and manage finances/legal matters, nursing-facility level of care, Medicaid financial eligibility, and an available trained attendant. Source: https://medicaid.utah.gov/ltc-2/pd/

**How to Best Connect**
Contact DSPD at 801-538-4200 to ask about referral, waiting list status, Medicaid financial screening, and waiver application steps.

**Access**
The waiver is statewide and designed to help people remain in their homes or other community settings. Services listed include financial management, personal assistance, personal emergency response, and specialized medical equipment/supplies.

**Important Information to Know**
The waiver serves a limited number of people and has a waiting list. Services are provided only if assessed as needed, and Medicaid/clinical approval is not guaranteed.
resources.name: Utah Medicaid and DSPD - Physical Disabilities Waiver

resources.address: PO Box 144720, Salt Lake City, UT 84114-4720
resources.description: Utah's statewide Baby Watch Early Intervention Program providing referral, free evaluation access, family coaching, and local Part C early intervention services for infants and toddlers with delays or disabilities.
resources.hours: Baby Watch state office Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; local contractor hours may vary.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Parents, guardians, or professionals concerned about an infant or toddler's development can refer to early intervention. Baby Watch supports infants and toddlers with developmental delays or disabilities; local evaluation determines eligibility. Source: https://familyhealth.utah.gov/oec/baby-watch-early-intervention/

**How to Best Connect**
Contact the local early intervention program for a free evaluation. For Salt Lake County, DHHS lists DDI Vantage for Granite, Murray, and Salt Lake school districts at 801-266-3939, and Jordan Child Development Center for Jordan and Canyons school districts at 801-567-8510. State Baby Watch: 801-273-2900 or 800-961-4226.

**Access**
Services use a family-coaching model in the child's natural environment, such as home or child care. The state Baby Watch office posts Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM; local program schedules vary.

**Important Information to Know**
Evaluation is free. Ongoing eligible services may involve Baby Watch family fees or billing; the state page links a family fee form and sliding fee scale. Confirm costs, IFSP services, and local provider assignment before relying on a start date.
resources.name: Utah DHHS - Baby Watch Early Intervention Program

resources.address: 6232 S 900 E, Murray, UT 84121
resources.description: Valley Behavioral Health adult autism/IDD day and learning program using ABA-informed support for daily living, community access, lifelong learning, vocational training, and supported employment opportunities.
resources.hours: Program hours were not published on the page; call Valley Access to confirm schedule and openings.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
The Adult Ability Center serves adults with autism or intellectual/developmental disabilities who need a high level of support, including people with lower cognitive and communication skills or challenging behavioral needs. Funding, clinical fit, and openings must be screened by Valley. Source: https://valleycares.com/adult-ability-center

**How to Best Connect**
Call Valley Behavioral Health at 888-949-4864 or 801-263-7100, or text 385-474-8887, and ask how to access the Adult Ability Center and autism/IDD services.

**Access**
The program is in Murray and focuses on community access, home living, social/leisure, fitness, vocational training, academics, library use, culinary skills, arts, agriculture, and healthcare-environment coping. Published hours and intake timelines were not listed; confirm before referral.

**Important Information to Know**
Public materials do not guarantee no-cost services. Expect screening for Medicaid, insurance, DSPD, or private-pay options, and verify current capacity and transportation arrangements.
resources.name: Valley Behavioral Health - Adult Ability Center of Lifetime Learning

resources.address: 5414 W Daybreak Pkwy, C-4 #433, South Jordan, UT 84009
resources.description: Statewide Children First Education Fund scholarship for Utah children with disabilities to help pay approved private school, homeschool, and special-needs service provider expenses.
resources.hours: Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
CFEF states scholarship applications are open for the 2026-27 school year for children with disabilities for private school and homeschool expenses. Specific qualification rules, documentation, award amounts, and deadlines must be checked in the parent documents/application portal. Source: https://cfe-fund.org/

**How to Best Connect**
Use the CFEF Apply Now link at https://cfe-fund.org/ or email info@childrenfirsteducationfund.org. Call 801-406-9080 with questions.

**Access**
This is statewide and application-based, not a walk-in service. CFEF posts Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM and a South Jordan mailing address.

**Important Information to Know**
Scholarship funding is not guaranteed. Families should confirm whether public/charter withdrawal, eligible expense documentation, reimbursement steps, and provider/school verification apply before making school or homeschool spending decisions.
resources.name: Children First Education Fund - Carson Smith Opportunity Scholarship

resources.address: 2001 S State Street, Suite S1-600, Salt Lake City, UT 84114
resources.description: Salt Lake County Alternatives Program phone-intake pathway for non-Medicaid in-home support and case management for adults 18+ needing help with activities of daily living and meeting financial limits.
resources.hours: County program hours were not published on the page; call for intake availability.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
The Alternatives Program is listed for adults age 18+ who can complete a phone intake reviewing ability to perform activities of daily living. Current county limits list single income up to $1,995/month and assets up to $6,000; married couple income up to $2,705/month and assets up to $12,000. Source: https://www.saltlakecounty.gov/aging-adult-services/services/home-community-based-care/

**How to Best Connect**
Call Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services Home & Community Based Care at 385-468-3200 and ask for TAP screening/intake.

**Access**
The program serves Salt Lake County and begins with phone intake. Services may include case management and coordination of in-home supports for people needing help with tasks such as shopping, meal preparation, transfers, dressing, or medication management.

**Important Information to Know**
Eligibility criteria vary by program and include age, medical condition, and finances. TAP is separate from Medicaid Aging Waiver and Veteran Directed Care; approval, service level, and provider availability are not guaranteed.
resources.name: Salt Lake County Aging & Adult Services - The Alternatives Program

resources.address: 511 W 200 S, #130, Salt Lake City, UT 84101
resources.description: Disability-focused arts access nonprofit offering opportunities for artists with disabilities, gallery/workshop space, accessibility education, and arts inclusion partnerships.
resources.hours: Open by appointment only when an exhibition is not on display; exhibition hours and program schedules vary.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Art Access increases accessibility to the arts through opportunities for artists with disabilities and education for community and cultural organizations. Specific program eligibility, artist calls, mentorships, and stipends vary by offering. Source: https://artaccessutah.org/

**How to Best Connect**
Email connect@artaccessutah.org for appointments or general questions, and sign up for Art Access updates/events through the website.

**Access**
Art Access lists its gallery/workshop space at 511 W 200 S, #130, Salt Lake City. The site says it is open by appointment only when an exhibition is not on display, and program schedules vary.

**Important Information to Know**
Confirm current exhibition hours, workshop schedules, artist opportunity deadlines, access accommodations, costs, and stipend details before referring. Breaking Barriers cultural accessibility training is also listed but primarily serves organizations rather than individual disability support needs.
resources.name: Art Access Utah - Disability Arts Access and Artist Opportunities

resources.address: PO Box 143106, Salt Lake City, UT 84114-3106
resources.description: Utah Medicaid state-plan Personal Care benefit covering approved in-home personal care for eligible Medicaid members through enrolled providers and required visit verification.
resources.hours: Medicaid eligibility/customer-service hours were not confirmed; call DWS or the member's Medicaid health plan.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Current Utah Medicaid materials list Personal Care as a covered Medicaid benefit, and EVV guidance lists personal care service codes. A member must be Medicaid-eligible and meet medical-necessity/provider-manual criteria; exact current criteria and physician order requirements should be confirmed with Utah Medicaid or the member's health plan. Sources: https://medicaid.utah.gov/medicaid-benefits/ and https://medicaid.utah.gov/evv/

**How to Best Connect**
Medicaid applicants can contact DWS eligibility at 866-435-7414. Existing Medicaid members should contact their health plan, Health Program Representative, or Medicaid provider to ask how to request Personal Care Services and prior authorization if needed.

**Access**
Services are statewide and delivered by Medicaid-enrolled providers in home/community settings when approved. Electronic Visit Verification is required for personal care services.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not an emergency caregiver program and not a guaranteed benefit without Medicaid eligibility, provider acceptance, and authorization. The consumer-facing page is limited, so confirm current medical criteria, covered tasks, hours, and provider availability before relying on the service.
resources.name: Utah Medicaid - State Plan Personal Care Services

resources.address: 500 Foothill Drive, Salt Lake City, UT 84148
resources.description: VA Salt Lake City enrolled-veteran disability support access point including prosthetics/sensory aids contact, caregiver support, recreation/adaptive sports therapy, and related rehabilitative services.
resources.hours: Main facility/service hours vary by clinic; call before visiting. Recreation/adaptive sports and caregiver support require VA contact or consult.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Services generally require VA health care enrollment and clinical/service eligibility. Adaptive sports outpatient programming lists veterans with SCI, MS, TBI, amputations, legal blindness/visual impairment, hemiparesis, ALS, Parkinson disease, stroke residuals, or other neurological disorders causing disabling neuromuscular function. Sources: https://www.va.gov/salt-lake-city-health-care/health-services/ and https://www.va.gov/salt-lake-city-health-care/programs/recreation-therapy/

**How to Best Connect**
Call the VA Salt Lake City main line at 801-582-1565. The contact page lists Prosthetics at ext. 1220. For Recreation Therapy Adaptive Sports, call 801-635-5047. Caregivers can use the VA Caregiver Support Line at 855-260-3274 or contact local caregiver coordinators through the VA Salt Lake caregiver support page.

**Access**
VA Salt Lake City serves enrolled veterans through the George E. Wahlen VA Medical Center and related clinics. Some services require a provider consult; outpatient recreation therapy explicitly says consults are needed for specific programs.

**Important Information to Know**
Availability, eligibility, HISA/home modification approvals, prosthetic items, stipends, and adaptive sports participation depend on VA rules, clinical need, funding, and documentation. This listing is not a guarantee of benefit approval.
resources.name: VA Salt Lake City Health Care - Disability Support Services

resources.address: 288 N 1460 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: State Office of Public Guardian guardianship and conservatorship services for adults unable to make basic life decisions who lack appropriate family or other support options.
resources.hours: Office hours were not published on the page; call before sending or visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
OPG serves adults unable to make basic life decisions due to conditions such as aging-related illness, intellectual disabilities, brain injuries, or mental illness, often when no family or friends can care for them or abuse/neglect/exploitation is involved. The referral instructions currently linked by OPG (dated 2022) specify Utah residence, age 18 or older, no willing and able family guardian, inability to afford a private guardian, serious risk, and no suitable less restrictive alternative. A clinical capacity assessment and court process are required; OPG does not conduct the capacity assessment itself. Confirm current screening requirements directly. Source: https://daas.utah.gov/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/Opg-referral-information-2022.docx-1.pdf Source: https://daas.utah.gov/office-of-public-guardian/

**How to Best Connect**
Follow the OPG referral instructions and submit the referral form by email, mail to 288 N 1460 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84116, or fax to 801-538-8243. Call 801-538-8255 with questions.

**Access**
This is a statewide DHHS program with a Salt Lake City office. Referral is document-based rather than walk-in immediate service.

**Important Information to Know**
OPG cannot accept every referral and continues efforts to locate/reunite individuals with family or close friends when appropriate. Guardianship/conservatorship is a legal decision-making pathway; legal advice should come from a qualified attorney or court resource.
resources.name: Utah DHHS Office of Public Guardian

resources.address: 195 N 1950 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: Utah EHDI newborn hearing-screening, CMV-testing, diagnostic audiology follow-up, early-intervention referral, and parent-to-parent support pathway for infants who are deaf or hard of hearing.
resources.hours: Program office hours were not confirmed; newborn screening and follow-up timelines are time-sensitive.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
EHDI applies to Utah newborns and infants needing hearing screening, repeat screening, diagnostic evaluation, CMV testing after failed screening, and early intervention referral when deaf or hard of hearing. Source: https://familyhealth.utah.gov/cshcn/ehdi/

**How to Best Connect**
Parents should work with the birth facility, pediatrician, pediatric audiologist, and Utah EHDI Program. Contact Utah EHDI at 801-273-6600 when guidance is needed, especially if CMV testing timelines or follow-up are uncertain.

**Access**
Utah goals include screening before hospital discharge or before 10 days of age for out-of-hospital births, repeat screening before 10 days if failed, diagnostic hearing evaluation before 3 months after a second failed screen, CMV testing before 21 days, and early intervention enrollment before 6 months if diagnosed.

**Important Information to Know**
EHDI is a screening, follow-up, referral, and care-coordination system, not a hearing-aid payer. Its state guidance also includes family referral to EHDI parent-to-parent support. Ask the program how to connect with that support. Source: https://familyhealth.utah.gov/cshcn/ehdi/ Time-sensitive CMV testing and pediatric audiology follow-up should not be delayed.
resources.name: Utah DHHS - Early Hearing Detection and Intervention

resources.address: 195 N 1950 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
resources.description: DSPD caregiver compensation option allowing eligible parents, step-parents, legal guardians, and spouses to be paid caregivers for people already receiving qualifying DSPD living-support services.
resources.hours: Program hours were not published; contact DSPD/support coordinator for current process.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
DSPD states caregiver compensation is an ongoing supported living service for people receiving DSPD services, allowing parents, step-parents, legal guardians, and spouses to be paid caregivers for individuals who qualify for living support. Source: https://dspd.utah.gov/caregiver-compensation/

**How to Best Connect**
Current DSPD participants should talk with their DSPD support coordinator/provider about caregiver compensation, required family training, forms, certifications, and model options.

**Access**
The DSPD page provides required training materials, knowledge-check instructions, medical/behavioral certification forms, monthly summary forms, and program guidance. Access is through the existing DSPD service plan rather than general public enrollment.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not available to all families of people with disabilities. It is limited to people already receiving qualifying DSPD living-support services, and hours/compensation depend on assessed need and program rules.
resources.name: Utah DSPD - Caregiver Compensation

resources.description: Free Utah Department of Veterans and Military Affairs accredited Veterans Service Officer help preparing, submitting, and appealing VA disability compensation, pension, and other benefits claims.
resources.hours: Appointment hours and office locations vary; schedule through UDVMA.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
UDVMA assists Utah veterans, service members, and eligible family members with VA benefits and claims. Disability compensation and pension outcomes depend on federal VA eligibility and evidence. Source: https://veterans.utah.gov/

**How to Best Connect**
Use the VA Claims Assistance scheduling link on the UDVMA site or call 801-326-2372 to connect with an accredited claims representative.

**Access**
The program is statewide and appointment-based. UDVMA states trained and accredited veteran service officers help prepare, submit, and appeal VA claims free of charge.

**Important Information to Know**
This is claims navigation, not emergency aid or a guarantee of VA approval. Ask what records to bring, including DD-214, medical evidence, prior VA letters, and identification.

resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
Utah Community Action Head Start/Early Head Start accepts applications for children ages 0-5 and prenatal services. Families at or below 100% of federal poverty level are eligible, and children with disabilities or foster children may still be eligible above poverty guidelines. Source: https://utahca.org/head-start-preschool/

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online through the Utah Community Action Head Start page in English or Spanish, then schedule the eligibility interview/phone appointment. For questions, call 801-359-2444.

**Access**
The program serves Salt Lake and Tooele Counties at multiple centers. It provides no-cost preschool/early childhood education, meals, health/dental/vision/hearing and developmental screenings, family support, and inclusive classrooms. UCA states it does not provide transportation but may assist with carpooling or bus/TRAX vouchers.

**Important Information to Know**
Utah Community Action states 10% of Head Start enrollment is reserved for children with disabilities and placement is not denied based on disability or severity. Classroom availability varies, and application/interview completion does not guarantee immediate placement.
resources.name: Utah Community Action - Inclusive Head Start and Early Head Start

resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
The Salt Lake City MS Support Group is for people living with multiple sclerosis and their family and friends. MS Navigator support is for MS-related questions and resource navigation. Source: https://www.nationalmssociety.org/how-you-can-help/get-involved/calendar-of-all-programs-and-events/salt-lake-city-ms-support-group

**How to Best Connect**
For the support group, contact the listed leader Serena at serenahawatmeh@gmail.com before attending to verify meeting date and location. For national MS Navigator support, contact the National MS Society at 800-344-4867.

**Access**
The local group is listed at Beans & Brews Coffee House, 5608 S 900 E, Murray, on the first Saturday of each month from 2:00-3:00 PM MT. National support is remote by phone/online.

**Important Information to Know**
The group is free, but attendees should bring funds for their own beverages/snacks. Meeting details can change, and National MS Society financial assistance or referrals are limited and not guaranteed.

Pingree serves children and adolescents with Autism Spectrum Disorder. The current Valley form asks for insurance provider and treatment type; clinical fit, age details, funding, and openings must be confirmed. Source: https://valleycares.com/pingree-autism-center

**How to Best Connect**
Fill out the online form on the Pingree page and select Autism Services under treatment type, or call 888-949-4864. Valley also lists a walk-in Children, Youth, and Family Clinic intake at 3725 S 4100 W, Suite 200, West Valley City on Tuesday or Wednesday between 9:00 AM and 3:00 PM.

Core services include benefit checks, consultations, family support/training, center-based ABA therapy, social skills, and case management. The Pingree center is at 780 S Guardsman Way in Salt Lake City; the walk-in intake site is in West Valley City.

resources.hours: Program hours were not published; call or email before a visit.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
The Adaptive Care Program is for individuals older than 3 who have a developmental disability and difficulty coping or cooperating in a medical setting beyond what is age appropriate. Source: https://intermountainhealthcare.org/childrens-health/support-services/child-life-services/adaptive-care

**How to Best Connect**
Call the Adaptive Care main line at 385-531-4168 or email the program through the address on the Intermountain page. Campus support numbers are 801-664-1290 for Primary Children's Salt Lake and 385-395-1593 for Lehi.

**Access**
Adaptive Care child life specialists create a care plan with families and share it with medical staff throughout Intermountain Health. Supports may include social stories, tours, avoiding crowded areas, communication supports, sensory supports, play/distraction, and exam/treatment support.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an accommodation/support program within Intermountain Children's Health, not a standalone therapy, home-care, or community personal-care benefit. Confirm eligibility, location coverage, and how the plan will be used before appointments.
resources.name: Intermountain Primary Children's Hospital - Adaptive Care Program

resources.hours: Clinic hours were not published on the page; appointments/referrals required.
resources.informationText:
**Eligibility Requirements**
UDAC evaluates infants, children, and teens with developmental disabilities or developmental concerns and provides developmental assessments, therapy, and ongoing care through child developmental, neuromotor, neonatal follow-up, and heart center neurodevelopment programs. Source: https://healthcare.utah.edu/pediatrics/programs-services/udac

**How to Best Connect**
Use the referral links on the UDAC page for the Child Development Program or Neonatal Follow-Up Program, or call University of Utah Health/Primary Children's pediatric specialty access to confirm the correct referral route.

**Access**
In-person visits are at Primary Children's Eccles Outpatient Services, Level 2, Station 4, 81 N Mario Capecchi Dr., Salt Lake City. UDAC states some telehealth evaluations are available, but the Heart Center Neurodevelopment Program does not offer virtual visits and out-of-state families may need in-person visits.

**Important Information to Know**
Referral, insurance/Medicaid acceptance, wait time, and clinic fit vary by program. UDAC can help establish developmental needs and care recommendations but does not guarantee school, Medicaid, DSPD, or other benefits.
resources.name: University of Utah Health and Primary Children's - University Developmental Assessment Clinics
